title.zh: 卷三十 志第十一: 禮三 宗廟 禘袷 朝享、時享儀
title.en: Volume 30 Treatises 11: Rites 3 - Ancestral Temples, Dijia, Worshipping, Seasonal Rituals
title.raw: 卷三十 志第十一: 禮三 宗廟 禘袷 朝享、時享儀 Volume 30 Treatises 11: Rites 3 - Ancestral Temples, Dijia, Worshipping, Seasonal Rituals

sentences.zh: 金初無宗廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jin there were no ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jin dynasty there were no ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年九月，太祖葬上京宮城之西南，建甯神殿於陵上，以時薦享。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Tianfu, Taizu was buried southwest of the palace city at Shangjing. Ningshen Hall was built atop the tomb, and seasonal offerings were presented there.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianfu 7, Taizu was buried southwest of the palace city at Shangjing. Ningshen Hall was erected on the tomb mound, where seasonal offerings were made.

sentences.zh: 自是諸京皆立廟，惟在京師者則曰太廟。

translations.literal: From then on temples were established in every capital; only the one in the imperial capital was called the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter temples were established in every capital, but only the one at the imperial seat was called the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，以宋二帝見太祖廟者，是也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui, when the two Song emperors were brought before Taizu's temple, this was such a case.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year of Tianhui, when the two captive Song emperors were presented at Taizu's temple, was one such instance.

sentences.zh: 或因遼之故廟，安置禦容，亦謂之廟。

translations.literal: Sometimes former Liao temples were used to install imperial portraits, and these too were called temples.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes former Liao temples were repurposed to house imperial portraits, and these were also called temples.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，熙宗幸燕及受尊號，皆親享恭謝，是也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan, when Xizong visited Yan and received his honorific title, he personally performed the rites of offering and thanksgiving on both occasions.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 3, when Xizong traveled to Yan and received his honorific title, he personally performed the offering and thanksgiving rites on both occasions.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年，初立太廟，八年，太廟成，則上京之廟也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangtong the Grand Ancestral Temple was first established; in the eighth year it was completed. This was the temple at Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 3 the Grand Ancestral Temple was first established, and it was completed in Huangtong 8. This was the temple at Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，海陵遷燕，乃增廣舊廟，奉遷祖宗神主於新都 ，三年十一月丁卯，奉安於太廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, when Hailing moved the capital to Yan, the old temple was enlarged and expanded. The spirit tablets of the ancestors were reverently transferred to the new capital. On dingmao, the eleventh month of the third year, they were installed in the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenyuan era, when Hailing moved the capital to Yan, the old temple was enlarged. The spirit tablets of the forebears were ceremonially transferred to the new capital, and on dingmao in 11/Zhenyuan 3 they were installed in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 正隆中，營建南京宮室，複立宗廟，南渡因之。

translations.literal: During Zhenglong, the palaces at the Southern Capital were built and the ancestral temple was re-established; this arrangement continued after the southward move.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenglong era the Southern Capital palaces were built and the ancestral temple was re-established, and this arrangement was retained after the court moved south.

sentences.zh: 其廟制，史不載，傳志雜記或可概見，今附之。

translations.literal: The temple system is not recorded in the official history, but may be seen in outline in miscellaneous notes and local gazetteers. These are appended here.
translations.idiomatic: The official history does not record the temple system in full, but miscellaneous notes and local gazetteers preserve something of it. These are appended here.

sentences.zh: 汴京之廟，在宮南馳道之東。

translations.literal: The temple at Bianjing stood east of the imperial roadway south of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The temple at Bianjing stood east of the imperial roadway south of the palace.

sentences.zh: 殿規，一屋四注，限其北為神室，其前為通廊。

translations.literal: The hall was designed as a single building with four-sloped eaves. Its northern section was designated the spirit chamber, and the area before it was a connecting corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The hall was a single structure with four-sloped eaves. The northern section formed the spirit chamber, with a connecting corridor in front.

sentences.zh: 東西二十六楹，為間二十有五，每間為一室。

translations.literal: East and west there were twenty-six bays, divided into twenty-five intervals, each interval forming one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: It had twenty-six bays east and west, divided into twenty-five intervals, each interval forming one chamber.

sentences.zh: 廟端各虛一間為夾室，中二十三間為十一室。

translations.literal: At each end of the temple one interval was left vacant as a side chamber; the central twenty-three intervals formed eleven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: At each end of the temple one interval was left open as a side chamber, while the central twenty-three intervals formed eleven chambers.

sentences.zh: 從西三間為一室，為始祖廟，祔德帝、安帝、獻祖、昭祖、景祖祧主五，餘皆兩間為一室。

translations.literal: Starting from the west, three intervals formed one chamber as the temple of the founding ancestor, enshrining the removed tablets of Emperor De, Emperor An, Xianzu, Zhaozu, and Jingzu—five in all. The remaining chambers each occupied two intervals.
translations.idiomatic: From the west, three intervals formed one chamber for the founding ancestor, enshrining the removed tablets of Emperors De and An and of Xianzu, Zhaozu, and Jingzu—five in all. The remaining chambers each occupied two intervals.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「惟第二、第二室兩間，餘止一間為一室，總十有七間。

translations.literal: Some say: 'Only the second and third chambers had two intervals each; the rest had only one interval per chamber, for a total of seventeen intervals.'
translations.idiomatic: Some say that only the second and third chambers had two intervals each, while the rest had one interval per chamber, for a total of seventeen intervals.

sentences.zh: 」世祖室祔肅宗，穆宗室祔康宗，餘皆無祔。

translations.literal: Shizu's chamber enshrined Suzong alongside; Muzong's chamber enshrined Kangzong alongside; the rest had no accompanying enshrinements.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's chamber had Suzong enshrined alongside; Muzong's chamber had Kangzong enshrined alongside; the rest had no accompanying enshrinements.

sentences.zh: 每室門一、牖一、門在左，牖在右，皆南向。

translations.literal: Each chamber had one door and one window; the door was on the left and the window on the right, both facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber had one door and one window—the door on the left, the window on the right—both facing south.

sentences.zh: 石室之龕於各室之西壁，東向。

translations.literal: Stone niches were set into the west wall of each chamber, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Stone niches were set into the west wall of each chamber, facing east.

sentences.zh: 其始祖之龕六，南向者五、東向者一，其二其三俱二龕，餘皆一室一龕，總十八龕。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor's chamber had six niches: five facing south and one facing east. The second and third chambers each had two niches; the rest had one niche per chamber, for a total of eighteen niches.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor's chamber had six niches—five facing south and one facing east. The second and third chambers each had two niches, and the rest one niche per chamber, for eighteen niches in all.

sentences.zh: 祭日出主於北墉下，南向。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice the spirit tablets were brought out below the north wall, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice the spirit tablets were brought out below the north wall, facing south.

sentences.zh: 禘祫則並出主，始祖東向，群主依昭穆南北相向，東西序列。

translations.literal: At di and jia rites all tablets were brought out together. The founding ancestor faced east; the other lords were arranged according to zhao and mu, facing north and south in pairs, arrayed east and west.
translations.idiomatic: At di and jia rites all tablets were brought out together. The founding ancestor faced east, while the other lords were arranged by zhao and mu precedence, facing north and south in pairs and arrayed east and west.

sentences.zh: 室戶外之通廊，殿階二級，列陛三，前井亭二。

translations.literal: Outside the chamber doors was a connecting corridor. The hall had two steps and three ranks of stairs, with two well pavilions in front.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the chamber doors ran a connecting corridor. The hall had two steps and three ranks of stairs, with two well pavilions in front.

sentences.zh: 外作重垣四繚，南東西皆有門。

translations.literal: Outside were four concentric enclosing walls, with gates on the south, east, and west.
translations.idiomatic: Outside were four concentric enclosing walls, with gates on the south, east, and west.

sentences.zh: 內垣之隅有樓，南門五闔，餘皆三。

translations.literal: At the corners of the inner enclosure were towers. The south gate had five leaves; the others had three.
translations.idiomatic: Towers stood at the corners of the inner enclosure. The south gate had five leaves; the others had three.

sentences.zh: 中垣之外東北，冊寶殿也，太常官一人季視其封緘，謂之點寶。

translations.literal: Northeast outside the middle enclosure was the Hall of Registers and Seals. One official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices inspected the seals each season; this was called 'checking the treasures.'
translations.idiomatic: Northeast outside the middle enclosure stood the Hall of Registers and Seals. One official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices inspected the seals each season in what was called 'checking the treasures.'

sentences.zh: 內垣之南曰大次，東南為神庖。

translations.literal: South of the inner enclosure was the great resting pavilion; southeast was the spirit kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: South of the inner enclosure was the great resting pavilion; to the southeast was the spirit kitchen.

sentences.zh: 廟門翼兩廡，各二十有五楹，為齋郎執事之次。

translations.literal: Flanking the temple gate were two side halls, each of twenty-five bays, serving as stations for the fasting officers on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking the temple gate were two side halls of twenty-five bays each, where the fasting officers on duty took their stations.

sentences.zh: 西南垣外，則廟署也。

translations.literal: Outside the southwest wall was the temple administration.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the southwest wall stood the temple administration.

sentences.zh: 神門列戟各二十有四，植以木錡。

translations.literal: At the spirit gate twenty-four halberds were displayed in rows, mounted on wooden stands.
translations.idiomatic: At the spirit gate twenty-four halberds were displayed in rows, mounted on wooden stands.

sentences.zh: 戟下以板為掌形，畫二青龍，下垂五色帶長五尺，享前一日則縣戟上，祭畢藏之。

translations.literal: Beneath each halberd was a palm-shaped board painted with two azure dragons, from which hung a five-colored sash five feet long. The day before the offering it was hung on the halberd; after the sacrifice it was stored away.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath each halberd was a palm-shaped board painted with two azure dragons, from which hung a five-colored sash five feet long. The day before the offering it was hung on the halberd and stored away again after the rite.

sentences.zh: 室次。

translations.literal: Order of the chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Order of the Chambers

sentences.zh: 大定十二年，議建閔宗別廟，禮官援晉惠、懷、唐中宗、後唐莊宗升祔故事，若依此典，武靈皇帝無嗣亦合升祔。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dading, when a separate temple for Emperor Min was under discussion, ritual officials cited the precedents of the Jin emperors Hui and Huai, Tang Zhongzong, and Later Tang Zhuangzong being elevated for enshrinement. If these precedents were followed, Emperor Wuling, who left no heir, would also qualify for elevation and enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 12, when a separate temple for Emperor Min was under discussion, ritual officials cited the precedents of Jin emperors Hui and Huai, Tang Zhongzong, and Later Tang Zhuangzong being elevated for enshrinement. On that precedent, Emperor Wuling, who left no heir, would also qualify for elevation and enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 然中宗之祔，始則為虛室，終增至九室。

translations.literal: Yet Zhongzong's enshrinement began with a vacant chamber and eventually expanded to nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhongzong's enshrinement had begun with a vacant chamber and eventually expanded to nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 惠、懷之祔乃遷豫章、穎川二廟、莊宗之祔乃祧懿祖一室。

translations.literal: The enshrinement of Hui and Huai required moving the temples of Yuzhang and Yingchuan; Zhuangzong's enshrinement required removing Yizu from one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The enshrinement of Hui and Huai required moving the temples of Yuzhang and Yingchuan, while Zhuangzong's enshrinement required removing Yizu from one chamber.

sentences.zh: 今太廟之制，除祧廟外，為七世十一室，如當升祔武靈，既須別祧一廟。

translations.literal: The present Grand Ancestral Temple system, apart from removed-line temples, comprises seven generations in eleven chambers. If Wuling were to be elevated for enshrinement, one temple from the removed line would have to be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present Grand Ancestral Temple system, apart from removed-line temples, there are seven generations in eleven chambers. If Wuling were to be elevated for enshrinement, one removed-line temple would have to be set aside.

sentences.zh: 《荀子》曰：「有天下者事七世。

translations.literal: The Xunzi says: 'One who possesses All Under Heaven serves seven generations.'
translations.idiomatic: The Xunzi says, 'One who possesses All Under Heaven serves seven generations.'

sentences.zh: 」若旁容兄弟，上毀祖考，則天子有不得事七世者矣。

translations.literal: If brothers were accommodated alongside and ancestors above were displaced, then the Son of Heaven would be unable to serve seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: If brothers were accommodated alongside and ancestors above were displaced, the Son of Heaven would no longer be able to serve seven generations.

sentences.zh: 伏睹宗廟世次，自睿宗上至始祖，凡七世，別無可祧之廟。

translations.literal: Observing the generational order of the ancestral temple, from Ruizong up to the founding ancestor there are seven generations, and there is no other temple that can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: The generational order of the ancestral temple runs from Ruizong up to the founding ancestor—seven generations in all—with no other temple available for removal.

sentences.zh: 《晉史》雲：「廟以容主為限，無拘常數。

translations.literal: The History of Jin states: 'The temple is limited by the number of spirit tablets it can hold, not by a fixed number.'
translations.idiomatic: The History of Jin states, 'The temple is limited by the number of spirit tablets it can hold, not by a fixed number.'

sentences.zh: 」東晉與唐皆用此制，遂增至十一室。

translations.literal: Both Eastern Jin and Tang used this system, and the number of chambers was eventually increased to eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Both Eastern Jin and Tang used this system, and the number of chambers was eventually increased to eleven.

sentences.zh: 康帝承統，以兄弟為一室，故不遷遠廟而祔成帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang succeeded to the throne, he and his brother shared one chamber, so the distant temple was not moved and Emperor Cheng was enshrined alongside.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Kang succeeded to the throne, he and his brother shared one chamber, so the distant temple was not moved and Emperor Cheng was enshrined alongside.

sentences.zh: 唐以敬、文、武三宗同為一代，於太廟東間增置兩室，定為九代十一室。

translations.literal: Tang treated Emperors Jing, Wen, and Wu as a single generation. Two chambers were added in the eastern section of the Grand Ancestral Temple, fixing the arrangement at nine generations in eleven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang treated Emperors Jing, Wen, and Wu as a single generation, added two chambers in the eastern section of the Grand Ancestral Temple, and fixed the arrangement at nine generations in eleven chambers.

sentences.zh: 今太廟已滿此數，如用不拘常數之說，增至十二室，可也。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestral Temple has already reached this number. If the principle of not being bound by a fixed count were applied, increasing it to twelve chambers would be permissible.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestral Temple has already reached this number. If the principle of not being bound by a fixed count were applied, increasing it to twelve chambers would be permissible.

sentences.zh: 然廟制已定，復議增展，其事甚重，又與睿宗皇帝祏室昭穆亦恐更改。

translations.literal: Yet the temple system is already fixed, and to reopen discussion of expansion is a weighty matter. It may also alter the zhao-mu placement of Emperor Ruizong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the temple system is already fixed, and reopening discussion of expansion is a weighty matter. It may also alter the zhao-mu placement of Emperor Ruizong's chamber.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義不以親親害尊尊，《漢志》雲：「父子不並坐，而孫可從王父。

translations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is not to let closeness of kin harm the precedence of rank. The Han Treatise states: 'Father and son do not sit together, but a grandson may follow his grandfather.'
translations.idiomatic: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is not to let closeness of kin harm the precedence of rank. The Han Treatise states, 'Father and son do not sit together, but a grandson may follow his grandfather.'

sentences.zh: 」若武靈升祔，太廟增作十二室。

translations.literal: If Wuling were elevated for enshrinement and the Grand Ancestral Temple expanded to twelve chambers,
translations.idiomatic: If Wuling were elevated for enshrinement and the Grand Ancestral Temple expanded to twelve chambers,

sentences.zh: 依春秋尊尊之典，武靈當在十一室，禘袷合食。

translations.literal: according to the Spring and Autumn principle of honoring rank, Wuling should occupy the eleventh chamber and share in the joint feasting at di and jia.
translations.idiomatic: then by the Spring and Autumn principle of honoring rank Wuling should occupy the eleventh chamber and share in the joint feasting at di and jia.

sentences.zh: 依孫從王父之典，當在太宗之下，而居昭位，又當稱宗。

translations.literal: According to the principle that a grandson follows his grandfather, he should be placed below Taizong yet occupy the zhao position, and should also be styled 'Zong.'
translations.idiomatic: By the principle that a grandson follows his grandfather, he should be placed below Taizong yet occupy the zhao position, and should also be styled 'Zong.'

sentences.zh: 然前升祔睿宗已在第十一室，累遇袷享，睿宗在穆位，與太宗昭位相對，若更改祏室及昭穆序，非有司所敢輕議，宜取聖裁。

translations.literal: Yet Ruizong had already been elevated for enshrinement in the eleventh chamber. At repeated jia offerings Ruizong occupied the mu position, facing Taizong in the zhao position. To alter the chamber placement and zhao-mu order is not something the responsible officials would dare decide lightly; the sage decision should be sought.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ruizong had already been elevated for enshrinement in the eleventh chamber. At repeated jia offerings Ruizong occupied the mu position, facing Taizong in the zhao position. Altering the chamber placement and zhao-mu order is not something the responsible officials would dare decide lightly; the imperial decision should be sought.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月，禘祔閔宗，遂增展太廟為十二室。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year, Emperor Min was enshrined at the di rite, and the Grand Ancestral Temple was expanded to twelve chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Dading 19, Emperor Min was enshrined at the di rite, and the Grand Ancestral Temple was expanded to twelve chambers.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，世宗將祔廟，有司言：「太廟十二室，自始祖至熙宗雖系八世。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, when Shizong was to be enshrined in the temple, the responsible officials said: 'The twelve chambers of the Grand Ancestral Temple, from the founding ancestor to Xizong, span eight generations.'
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29, when Shizong was to be enshrined in the temple, the responsible officials said, 'The Grand Ancestral Temple's twelve chambers, from the founding ancestor to Xizong, span eight generations.'

sentences.zh: 然世宗與熙宗為兄弟，不相為後，用晉成帝故事，止系七世，若特升世宗、顯宗即系九世。

translations.literal: Yet Shizong and Xizong were brothers who did not succeed one another. Following the precedent of Jin Emperor Cheng, this counts as only seven generations. If Shizong and Xianzong were specially elevated, it would count as nine generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shizong and Xizong were brothers who did not succeed one another. Following the precedent of Jin Emperor Cheng, this counts as only seven generations; if Shizong and Xianzong were specially elevated, it would count as nine.

sentences.zh: 」於是五月遂祧獻祖、昭祖，升祔世宗、明德皇后，顯宗於廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon, in the fifth month, Xianzu and Zhaozu were removed from the main line. Shizong, Empress Mingde, and Xianzong were elevated for enshrinement in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, in the fifth month, Xianzu and Zhaozu were removed from the main line, and Shizong, Empress Mingde, and Xianzong were elevated for enshrinement in the temple.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，宣宗南遷，廟社諸祀並委中都，自抹拈盡忠棄城南奔，時謁之禮盡廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when Xuanzong moved south, the temple, altars, and all sacrifices were entrusted to the Central Capital. From the time Moqian Jingzhong abandoned the city and fled south, the rites of audience were entirely abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2, when Xuanzong moved south, the temple, altars, and all sacrifices were left in the charge of the Central Capital. From the time Moqian Jingzhong abandoned the city and fled south, the rites of audience were entirely abandoned.

sentences.zh: 四年，禮官言：「廟社國之大事，今主上駐蹕陪京，列聖神主已遷於此，宜重修太廟社稷，以奉歲時之祭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, ritual officials said: 'The temple and altars are great affairs of state. The sovereign now resides at the accompanying capital, and the spirit tablets of the successive sages have been transferred here. The Grand Ancestral Temple and altars of soil and grain should be rebuilt to support the seasonal sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, ritual officials said, 'The temple and altars are great affairs of state. The sovereign now resides at the accompanying capital, and the spirit tablets of the successive sages have been transferred here. The Grand Ancestral Temple and altars of soil and grain should be rebuilt to support the seasonal sacrifices.'

sentences.zh: 按中都廟制，自始祖至章宗凡十二室，而今廟室止十一，若增建恐難卒成。

translations.literal: According to the temple system at the Central Capital, from the founding ancestor to Zhangzong there were twelve chambers in all, but the present temple has only eleven. New construction would probably be difficult to complete quickly.
translations.idiomatic: According to the temple system at the Central Capital, from the founding ancestor to Zhangzong there should be twelve chambers, but the present temple has only eleven. New construction would probably be difficult to complete quickly.

sentences.zh: 況時方多故，禮宜從變，今擬權祔肅宗主世祖室，始祖以下諸神主於隨室奉安。

translations.literal: Moreover, the times are troubled and ritual should adapt accordingly. It is now proposed provisionally to enshrine Suzong's tablet in Shizu's chamber, and to install the spirit tablets from the founding ancestor downward in the chambers as space allows.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the times are troubled and ritual should adapt accordingly. It is now proposed provisionally to enshrine Suzong's tablet in Shizu's chamber and to install the spirit tablets from the founding ancestor downward in the chambers as space allows.

sentences.zh: 」主用栗，依唐制，皇統九年所定也。

translations.literal: The tablets were made of chestnut wood, following the Tang system as fixed in the ninth year of Huangtong.
translations.idiomatic: The tablets were made of chestnut wood, following the Tang system as fixed in Huangtong 9.

sentences.zh: 祏室，旁及上下皆石，門東向，以木為闔，髹以硃。

translations.literal: The spirit chambers were stone on the sides, top, and bottom. The door faced east and was made of wood, lacquered vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit chambers were stone on the sides, top, and bottom. The door faced east, was made of wood, and was lacquered vermilion.

sentences.zh: 室中有褥，奠主訖，帝主居左，覆以黃羅帕，後主居右，覆以紅羅帕。

translations.literal: Inside each chamber was a cushion. After the tablets were placed, the senior tablet was on the left, covered with a yellow silk cloth; the junior tablet was on the right, covered with a red silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Inside each chamber was a cushion. After the tablets were placed, the senior tablet stood on the left under a yellow silk cloth, and the junior tablet on the right under a red silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 黼扆。

translations.literal: The embroidered screen.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Screen

sentences.zh: 以紙，木為筐，兩足如立屏狀。

translations.literal: It was made of paper and wood in a frame with two legs, shaped like a standing screen.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of paper and wood in a frame with two legs, shaped like a standing screen.

sentences.zh: 覆以紅羅三幅，繡金斧五十四，裹以紅絹，覆於屏上，其半無文者垂於其後。

translations.literal: It was covered with three panels of red silk embroidered with fifty-four golden axes, wrapped in red gauze and draped over the screen; the half without pattern hung down behind.
translations.idiomatic: It was covered with three panels of red silk embroidered with fifty-four golden axes, wrapped in red gauze and draped over the screen, with the undecorated half hanging down behind.

sentences.zh: 置北墉下，南向，前設几筵以坐神主。

translations.literal: It was placed below the north wall, facing south, with tables and mats set before it to seat the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: It was placed below the north wall, facing south, with tables and mats set before it to seat the spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 五席，各長五尺五寸，闊二尺五寸。

translations.literal: There were five mats, each five feet five inches long and two feet five inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: There were five mats, each five feet five inches long and two feet five inches wide.

sentences.zh: 莞筵，粉純。

translations.literal: Rush mat with white border.
translations.idiomatic: Rush mat with white border

sentences.zh: 以藺為席，緣以紅羅，以白繡蕙文及雲氣之狀，複以紅絹裹之。

translations.literal: The mat was made of sedge, bordered with red silk and embroidered in white with orchid patterns and cloud motifs, then wrapped again in red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: The mat was made of sedge, bordered with red silk and embroidered in white with orchid patterns and cloud motifs, then wrapped again in red gauze.

sentences.zh: 每位二。

translations.literal: Two for each tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Two for each tablet.

sentences.zh: 繅席，畫純。

translations.literal: Silk-woven mat with painted border.
translations.idiomatic: Silk-woven mat with painted border

sentences.zh: 以五色絨織青蒲為之，緣以紅羅，畫藻文及雲氣狀，亦以紅絹裹之。

translations.literal: It was woven in five-colored pile velvet with green rushes, bordered with red silk and painted with aquatic patterns and cloud motifs, also wrapped in red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: It was woven in five-colored pile velvet with green rushes, bordered with red silk and painted with aquatic patterns and cloud motifs, and also wrapped in red gauze.

sentences.zh: 每位二，在莞上。

translations.literal: Two for each tablet, placed atop the rush mat.
translations.idiomatic: Two for each tablet, placed atop the rush mat.

sentences.zh: 次席，黼純。

translations.literal: Secondary mat with embroidered border.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary mat with embroidered border

sentences.zh: 以輕筠為之，亦曰桃枝席，緣以紅綃，繡鐵色斧，裹以紅絹。

translations.literal: It was made of light bamboo, also called the peach-branch mat, bordered with red silk gauze and embroidered with iron-colored axes, wrapped in red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of light bamboo, also called the peach-branch mat, bordered with red silk gauze and embroidered with iron-colored axes, and wrapped in red gauze.

sentences.zh: 每位二，在繅席上。

translations.literal: Two for each tablet, placed atop the silk-woven mat.
translations.idiomatic: Two for each tablet, placed atop the silk-woven mat.

sentences.zh: 虎席二，大者長同，惟闊增一尺。

translations.literal: There were two tiger-skin mats. The larger was the same length but one foot wider.
translations.idiomatic: There were two tiger-skin mats. The larger was the same length but one foot wider.

sentences.zh: 以虎皮為褥，有厓，以紅羅繡金色斧緣之。

translations.literal: They were made of tiger hide as cushions, with raised edges bordered in red silk embroidered with golden axes.
translations.idiomatic: They were made of tiger hide as cushions, with raised edges bordered in red silk embroidered with golden axes.

sentences.zh: 又有小虎皮褥，制同三席。

translations.literal: There were also small tiger-skin cushions, made to the same specification as the three mats.
translations.idiomatic: There were also small tiger-skin cushions, made to the same specification as the three mats.

sentences.zh: 時喧則用桃枝次席，時寒則去桃枝加虎皮褥。

translations.literal: In warm weather the peach-branch secondary mat was used; in cold weather the peach-branch mat was removed and tiger-skin cushions were added.
translations.idiomatic: In warm weather the peach-branch secondary mat was used; in cold weather the peach-branch mat was removed and tiger-skin cushions were added.

sentences.zh: 夏、秋享，則用桃枝次席。

translations.literal: For summer and autumn offerings, the peach-branch secondary mat was used.
translations.idiomatic: For summer and autumn offerings, the peach-branch secondary mat was used.

sentences.zh: 二冬，則去桃枝加小虎皮褥于繅席上。

translations.literal: In the two winter months, the peach-branch mat was removed and small tiger-skin cushions were added atop the silk-woven mat.
translations.idiomatic: In the two winter months, the peach-branch mat was removed and small tiger-skin cushions were added atop the silk-woven mat.

sentences.zh: 臘冬，則又添大虎皮褥二于繅席上，遷小虎皮褥二在大褥之上。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, two large tiger-skin cushions were added atop the silk-woven mat, and the two small tiger-skin cushions were moved on top of the large ones.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, two large tiger-skin cushions were added atop the silk-woven mat, and the two small tiger-skin cushions were moved on top of the large ones.

sentences.zh: 曲幾三足，直幾二足，各長尺五寸，以丹漆之。

translations.literal: Curved tables had three legs and straight tables had two legs; each was one foot five inches long and lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: Curved tables had three legs and straight tables had two legs; each was one foot five inches long and lacquered red.

sentences.zh: 帝主前設曲幾，後設直幾。

translations.literal: Before the senior tablet a curved table was set; behind it a straight table.
translations.idiomatic: Before the senior tablet a curved table was set; behind it a straight table.

sentences.zh: 大定十一年，尚書省奏禘祫之儀曰：「《禮緯》：'三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading, the Department of State Affairs memorialized on the rites of di and jia, saying: 'The Ritual Apocrypha states: "Once every three years a jia; once every five years a di."'
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 11, the Department of State Affairs memorialized on the rites of di and jia, saying, 'The Ritual Apocrypha states, "Once every three years a jia; once every five years a di."'

sentences.zh: '唐開元中，太常議，禘祫之禮皆為殷祭，祫為合食祖廟，禘謂禘序尊卑。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era of Tang, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated that both di and jia rites were great offerings: jia meant joint feasting in the ancestral temple; di meant ordering precedence by rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Kaiyuan era, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that both di and jia rites were great offerings: jia meant joint feasting in the ancestral temple, and di meant ordering precedence by rank.

sentences.zh: 申先君逮下之慈，成群嗣奉親之孝。

translations.literal: They express the former lord's kindness in reaching down, and the assembled heirs' filial devotion in serving their forebears.
translations.idiomatic: They express the former lord's kindness in reaching down, and the assembled heirs' filial devotion in serving their forebears.

sentences.zh: 自異常享，有時行之。

translations.literal: Apart from the regular offerings, they were sometimes performed.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the regular offerings, they were sometimes performed.

sentences.zh: 祭不欲數，數則黷。

translations.literal: Sacrifices should not be too frequent; frequency leads to irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices should not be too frequent; frequency leads to irreverence.

sentences.zh: 不欲疏，疏則怠。

translations.literal: They should not be too sparse; sparseness leads to neglect.
translations.idiomatic: They should not be too sparse; sparseness leads to neglect.

sentences.zh: 是以王者法諸天道，以制祀典，丞嘗象時，禘祫象閏。

translations.literal: Therefore the king modeled himself on Heaven's Way in establishing the sacrificial canon: the spring and autumn offerings corresponded to the seasons; di and jia corresponded to the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the king modeled himself on Heaven's Way in establishing the sacrificial canon: the spring and autumn offerings corresponded to the seasons, and di and jia corresponded to the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 五歲再閏，天道大成，宗廟法之，再為殷祭。

translations.literal: Twice in five years there is an intercalary month; when Heaven's Way reaches completion, the ancestral temple follows it with two great offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Twice in five years there is an intercalary month; when Heaven's Way reaches completion, the ancestral temple follows it with two great offerings.

sentences.zh: 自周以後，並用此禮。

translations.literal: From Zhou onward, all used this ritual.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou onward, all used this ritual.

sentences.zh: 自大定九年已行祫禮，若議禘祭，當於袷後十八月孟夏行禮。

translations.literal: Since the jia rite had already been performed in the ninth year of Dading, if a di offering were to be discussed, it should be performed in the first month of summer, eighteen months after the jia.
translations.idiomatic: Since the jia rite had already been performed in Dading 9, if a di offering were to be discussed, it should be performed in the first month of summer, eighteen months after the jia.

sentences.zh: 」詔以「三年冬祫、五年夏禘」為常禮。

translations.literal: An edict fixed as the regular practice 'jia in winter of the third year, di in summer of the fifth year.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed as the regular practice 'jia in winter of the third year, di in summer of the fifth year.'

sentences.zh: 又言：「海陵時，每歲止以二月、十月遣使兩享，三年祫享。

translations.literal: It was further stated: 'During Hailing's time, each year offerings were dispatched only twice, in the second and tenth months, with a jia offering every three years.'
translations.idiomatic: It was further stated, 'During Hailing's time, offerings were dispatched only twice each year, in the second and tenth months, with a jia offering every three years.'

sentences.zh: 按唐禮四時各以孟月享于太廟，季冬又臘享，歲凡五享。

translations.literal: According to Tang ritual, offerings were made in the Grand Ancestral Temple in the first month of each season, with an additional la offering in the last month of winter, for five offerings in all each year.
translations.idiomatic: According to Tang ritual, offerings were made in the Grand Ancestral Temple in the first month of each season, with an additional la offering in the last month of winter, for five offerings in all each year.

sentences.zh: 若依海陵時歲止兩享，非天子之禮，宜從典禮歲五享。

translations.literal: If Hailing's practice of only two offerings per year were followed, this would not be the ritual of the Son of Heaven. The canonical practice of five offerings per year should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: If Hailing's practice of only two offerings per year were followed, this would not be the ritual of the Son of Heaven. The canonical practice of five offerings per year should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 享日並出神主前廊，序列昭穆。

translations.literal: On the day of offering all spirit tablets were brought out to the front corridor and arranged according to zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of offering all spirit tablets were brought out to the front corridor and arranged according to zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 應圖功臣配享廟廷，各配所事之廟，以位次為序。

translations.literal: Merit ministers of the approved chart received paired enjoyment in the temple court, each paired with the temple he had served, ordered by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers inscribed on the imperial commendation roll received paired offerings in the temple court, each accorded the temple he had served, arranged in order of rank.

sentences.zh: 以太子為亞獻，親王為終獻，或並用親王。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince served as secondary offerer and an imperial prince as final offerer, or imperial princes were used for both.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince served as secondary offerer and an imperial prince as final offerer—or imperial princes could fill both roles.

sentences.zh: 或以太尉為亞獻，光祿卿為終獻。

translations.literal: Or the Grand Commandant served as secondary offerer and the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, the Grand Commandant served as secondary offerer and the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 其月則停時享。

translations.literal: In that month the seasonal offerings were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: During that month the seasonal offerings were suspended.

sentences.zh: 儀闕。

translations.literal: The ritual account is incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual account is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 朝享儀

translations.literal: Ritual for the Morning Offering
translations.idiomatic: Ritual for the Morning Offering

sentences.zh: 大定十一年十一月，郊祀前一日，朝享太廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Dading, on the day before the suburban sacrifice, a morning offering was made at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Dading 11, on the day before the suburban sacrifice, a morning offering was made at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 齋戒如親郊。

translations.literal: Purification and fasting were as for personally performing the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Purification and fasting followed the same rules as for the emperor's personal suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 享前三日，太廟令帥其屬，掃除廟之內外。

translations.literal: Three days before the offering, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his subordinates to sweep clean inside and outside the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the offering, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his staff in sweeping the temple inside and out.

sentences.zh: 點檢司於廟之前約度，設兵衛旗幟。

translations.literal: The Inspection Office measured and laid out the area before the temple and set up military guards, banners, and flags.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspection Office measured out the ground before the temple and posted military guards with banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 尚舍于南神門之西設饌幔十一，南向，以西為上。

translations.literal: The Director of Accommodations set up eleven food pavilions west of the South Spirit Gate, facing south, with west as the superior position.
translations.idiomatic: West of the South Spirit Gate, the Director of Accommodations erected eleven food pavilions facing south, with the westernmost seat regarded as highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 殿中監帥尚舍，陳設大次殿。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Affairs led the Director of Accommodations in setting up the grand rest pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Palace Affairs supervised the Director of Accommodations in arranging the grand rest pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又設小次於阼階下，稍南，西向。

translations.literal: A small rest pavilion was also set up below the eastern steps, slightly to the south, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: A smaller rest pavilion was also set below the eastern steps, a little to the south, facing west.

sentences.zh: 又設皇帝拜褥位殿上，版位稍西。

translations.literal: The emperor's kneeling cushion was also set on the hall floor, with the tablet position slightly to the west.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall floor they also placed the emperor's kneeling cushion, with his tablet position slightly to the west.

sentences.zh: 又設黃道褥於廟門之內外，自玉輅至升輦之所，又自大次至東神門。

translations.literal: Yellow path mats were also laid inside and outside the temple gate, from the jade chariot to the place of mounting the palanquin, and from the grand rest pavilion to the East Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow path mats were also laid inside and outside the temple gate, from the jade chariot to the place where the palanquin was mounted, and from the grand rest pavilion to the East Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 又設七祀位一于殿下橫街之北，西街之西，東向，配享功臣位於殿下道東，橫街之南，西向，北上。

translations.literal: One position for the seven sacrifices was set north of the cross street below the hall, west of West Street, facing east; positions for accompanying merit ministers were east of the path below the hall, south of the cross street, facing west, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: One station for the seven sacrifices was placed north of the cross street below the hall, west of West Street, facing east; stations for accompanying merit ministers were placed east of the path below the hall, south of the cross street, facing west, with the northernmost seat highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 前二日，大樂令設宮縣之樂於庭中，四方各設編鐘三、編磬三。

translations.literal: Two days before, the Director of Great Music set up court ensemble music in the courtyard; on each of the four sides three chime bells and three stone chimes were set up.
translations.idiomatic: Two days beforehand, the Director of Great Music arranged the court ensemble in the courtyard, placing three chime bells and three stone chimes on each of the four sides.

sentences.zh: 東方編鐘起北，編磬間之，東向。

translations.literal: In the east the chime bells began from the north, with stone chimes interspersed among them, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: In the east the chime bells started from the north, with stone chimes placed between them, all facing east.

sentences.zh: 西方編磬起北，編鐘間之，西向。

translations.literal: In the west the stone chimes began from the north, with chime bells interspersed among them, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the west the stone chimes started from the north, with chime bells placed between them, all facing west.

sentences.zh: 南方編磬起西，編鐘間之，北方編鐘起西，編磬間之，俱北向。

translations.literal: In the south the stone chimes began from the west, with chime bells interspersed; in the north the chime bells began from the west, with stone chimes interspersed; all faced north.
translations.idiomatic: In the south the stone chimes started from the west with chime bells between them; in the north the chime bells started from the west with stone chimes between them; both groups faced north.

sentences.zh: 設特磬、大鐘、穀鐘共十二，於編縣之內，各依辰位。

translations.literal: Twelve special chimes, great bells, and grain bells were set up within the arranged ensemble, each according to its celestial position.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve special chimes, great bells, and grain bells were placed within the arranged ensemble, each positioned according to its corresponding celestial station.

sentences.zh: 樹路鼓、路鞀於北縣之內，道之左右。

translations.literal: Road drums and road taos were erected within the northern ensemble, to the left and right of the path.
translations.idiomatic: Road drums and road taos were erected within the northern ensemble, on either side of the path.

sentences.zh: 晉鼓一，在其後稍南。

translations.literal: One Jin drum was placed behind them, slightly to the south.
translations.idiomatic: One Jin drum was placed behind them, a little farther south.

sentences.zh: 植建鼓、鞞鼓、應鼓於四隅，建鼓在中，鞞鼓在左，應鼓在右，置柷敔於縣內，柷一在道東，敔一在道西。

translations.literal: Establishment drums, side drums, and response drums were planted at the four corners; the establishment drum in the center, the side drum on the left, the response drum on the right. Zhu and Yu were placed within the ensemble—one Zhu east of the path, one Yu west of the path.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment drums, side drums, and response drums were set at the four corners—the establishment drum in the center, the side drum on the left, and the response drum on the right. Within the ensemble one Zhu was placed east of the path and one Yu west of the path.

sentences.zh: 立舞表於酂綴之間。

translations.literal: Markers for standing dance were erected between the Cuò and Zhuì stations.
translations.idiomatic: Markers for the standing dance were set up between the Cuò and Zhuì stations.

sentences.zh: 設登歌之樂於殿上前楹間，金鐘一在東，太磬一在西，俱北向。

translations.literal: Ascending-song music was set between the front columns on the hall; one golden bell in the east, one great stone chime in the west, both facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The ascending-song ensemble was placed between the front columns of the hall—one golden bell in the east and one great stone chime in the west, both facing north.

sentences.zh: 柷一在金鐘北稍西，敔一在玉磬北稍東。

translations.literal: One Zhu was placed slightly west of north of the golden bell; one Yu slightly east of north of the jade chime.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhu stood slightly northwest of the golden bell, and one Yu slightly northeast of the jade chime.

sentences.zh: 搏拊二，一在柷北，一在敔北，東西相向。

translations.literal: Two clappers, one north of the Zhu and one north of the Yu, faced each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two clappers were placed—one north of the Zhu and one north of the Yu—facing each other across the east-west axis.

sentences.zh: 琴瑟在前。

translations.literal: Zithers and lutes were placed in front.
translations.idiomatic: Zithers and lutes were placed in front.

sentences.zh: 其匏竹者立於階間，重行北向。

translations.literal: The wind and bamboo instruments stood between the steps in double rows, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The wind and bamboo instruments stood between the steps in double rows, all facing north.

sentences.zh: 諸工人各位于縣後。

translations.literal: All musicians took their positions behind the ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: All the musicians took their positions behind the ensemble.

sentences.zh: 前一日，太廟令開室，奉禮郎帥其屬，設神位於每室內北墉下。

translations.literal: The day before, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple opened the chambers; the Ritual Gentleman led his subordinates to set up spirit positions at the base of the north wall in each chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the preceding day the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple opened the chambers, and the Ritual Gentleman led his staff in setting up spirit seats at the foot of the north wall in each chamber.

sentences.zh: 各設黼扆一、莞席一、繅席二、次席二、紫綾厚褥一、紫綾蒙褥一、曲幾一、直幾一。

translations.literal: For each were set one embroidered screen, one cattail mat, two silk-padded mats, two secondary mats, one thick purple silk cushion, one purple silk cover cushion, one curved table, and one straight table.
translations.idiomatic: At each seat they placed one embroidered screen, one cattail mat, two silk-padded mats, two secondary mats, one thick purple silk cushion, one purple silk cover cushion, one curved table, and one straight table.

sentences.zh: 又設皇帝版位於殿東間門內，西向。

translations.literal: The emperor's tablet position was also set inside the east chamber door, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: They also set the emperor's tablet position inside the east chamber door, facing west.

sentences.zh: 又設飲福位於東序，西向。

translations.literal: The position for receiving blessing was also set in the eastern wing, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The seat for receiving blessing was also placed in the eastern wing, facing west.

sentences.zh: 又設亞終獻位於殿下橫街之北稍東，西向。

translations.literal: Positions for the secondary and final offerers were also set slightly east of north of the cross street below the hall, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Seats for the secondary and final offerers were also placed slightly east of the cross street north of the hall, facing west.

sentences.zh: 助祭親王宗室使相位在亞終獻之後，助祭宗室位在橫街之南，西向。

translations.literal: Positions for assisting imperial princes and clan envoys were behind the secondary and final offerers; positions for assisting clansmen were south of the cross street, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Seats for assisting imperial princes and clan envoys were placed behind the secondary and final offerers, while seats for assisting clansmen were south of the cross street, facing west.

sentences.zh: 奉瓚官、奉瓚盤官、進爵酒官、奉爵官等又在其南，奉匜槃巾篚官位於其後。

translations.literal: The jade cup bearer, jade cup tray bearer, wine-presenting officer, wine-cup bearer, and others were further south; the ewer, tray, cloth, and basket bearers were behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The jade cup bearer, jade cup tray bearer, wine-presenting officer, wine-cup bearer, and others stood farther south, with the ewer, tray, cloth, and basket bearers behind them.

sentences.zh: 七祀獻官位在奉爵官之南，助奠讀祝奉罍洗爵洗等官位於其後。

translations.literal: Positions for the seven sacrifices offering officers were south of the wine-cup bearers; officers assisting presentation, reading prayers, and bearing urns and cup-washing vessels were behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Officers presenting offerings to the seven sacrifices stood south of the wine-cup bearers, with those assisting presentation, reading prayers, and bearing urns and cup-washing vessels behind them.

sentences.zh: 司尊彝官位在七祀獻官之南，亞終獻司罍洗爵洗奉爵酒官等又在其南，並西向，北上。

translations.literal: Positions for the vessel custodian officers were south of the seven sacrifices offering officers; officers for the secondary and final offerers who managed urn washing, cup washing, and wine presentation were further south; all faced west, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel custodians stood south of the seven sacrifices offering officers, and the secondary and final offerers' urn-washing, cup-washing, and wine officers stood farther south; all faced west, with the northernmost seat highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 大禮使位於西階之西稍南，與亞終獻相對。

translations.literal: The Grand Ritual Envoy stood slightly south of west of the western steps, opposite the secondary and final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ritual Envoy took his place slightly south of the western steps, facing the secondary and final offerers.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒，助祭宰相位在大禮使之南，侍中、執政官又在其南，禮部尚書、太常卿、太僕卿、光祿卿、功臣獻官在西，舉冊、光祿丞、太常博士又在其西，功臣助奠罍洗爵洗等官位於功臣獻官之後。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant and Minister over the Masses, and assisting chief ministers, stood south of the Grand Ritual Envoy; the Palace Attendant and chief administrators were further south. The Minister of Rites, Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Imperial Stud, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and merit ministers' offering officers were to the west; officers holding the register, the Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and Imperial Sacrifices academicians were further west; officers assisting merit ministers with presentation, urn washing, and cup washing stood behind the merit ministers' offering officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant and Minister over the Masses, together with the assisting chief ministers, stood south of the Grand Ritual Envoy, with the Palace Attendant and chief administrators farther south. To the west were the Minister of Rites, Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Imperial Stud, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and the merit ministers' offering officers; farther west were the register bearer, Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and Imperial Sacrifices academicians; and behind the merit ministers' offering officers stood those assisting with presentation, urn washing, and cup washing.

sentences.zh: 又設監祭御史位二於西階下，俱東向，北上。

translations.literal: Two supervising censor positions were also set below the western steps, both facing east, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising censor stations were also placed below the western steps, both facing east, with the northernmost seat highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎、太廟令、太官令、太祝、宮闈令、祝史位於亞獻終獻奉爵酒官之南，薦籩豆簠簋官、薦俎齋郎又在太祝、奉禮郎之南。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman, Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, Director of the Imperial Kitchen, Chief Invoker, Director of Palace Environs, and invoker scribes stood south of the secondary and final offerers' wine officers; officers presenting baskets, beans, grain vessels, and trays, and offering-attendants, were further south of the Chief Invoker and Ritual Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman, Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, Director of the Imperial Kitchen, Chief Invoker, Director of Palace Environs, and invoker scribes stood south of the secondary and final offerers' wine officers; officers presenting baskets, beans, grain vessels, and trays, together with the offering-attendants, stood farther south of the Chief Invoker and Ritual Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太廟丞、太官丞各位於令後。

translations.literal: The Vice Directors of the Grand Ancestral Temple and Imperial Kitchen each took his position behind his director.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Directors of the Grand Ancestral Temple and Imperial Kitchen each took his place behind his director.

sentences.zh: 協律郎位二，一於殿上前楹間，一于宮縣之西北，俱東向。

translations.literal: Two pitch-regulating officers: one between the front columns on the hall, one northwest of the court ensemble; both faced east.
translations.idiomatic: Two pitch-regulating officers were posted—one between the front columns of the hall and one northwest of the court ensemble—both facing east.

sentences.zh: 大樂令于登歌樂縣之北，大司樂於宮縣之北，良醖令於酌尊所，俱北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Great Music stood north of the ascending-song ensemble, the Grand Master of Music north of the court ensemble, and the Director of Fine Brew north of the libation vessels; all faced north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Great Music stood north of the ascending-song ensemble, the Grand Master of Music north of the court ensemble, and the Director of Fine Brew by the libation vessels; all faced north.

sentences.zh: 又設助祭文武群官位於橫街之南，東向北上。

translations.literal: Positions for assisting civil and military officials were also set south of the cross street, facing east, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Seats for the assisting civil and military officials were also placed south of the cross street, facing east, with the northernmost seat highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 又設光祿卿陳牲位於東神門外橫街之東，西向，以南為上。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices' position for displaying the sacrificial animals was also set east of the cross street outside the East Spirit Gate, facing west, with south as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices' station for displaying the sacrificial animals was also placed east of the cross street outside the East Spirit Gate, facing west, with the southernmost seat highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 設廩犧令位於牲西南，北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Sacrificial Livestock's position was set southwest of the sacrificial animals, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Livestock took his place southwest of the sacrificial animals, facing north.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝位於牲東，各當牲後，祝史各陪其後，俱西向。

translations.literal: All Chief Invokers stood east of the sacrificial animals, each aligned behind his animal; invoker scribes accompanied each behind him; all faced west.
translations.idiomatic: All the Chief Invokers stood east of the sacrificial animals, each aligned behind his animal, with invoker scribes accompanying them; all faced west.

sentences.zh: 設禮部尚書省牲位於牲前稍北，又設御史位於禮部尚書之西，俱南向。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites' position for inspecting the sacrificial animals was set slightly north of the animals' front; a censor's position was also set west of the Minister of Rites; both faced south.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites' station for inspecting the sacrificial animals was placed slightly north of the animals' forequarters, with a censor's station west of the Minister of Rites; both faced south.

sentences.zh: 禮部帥其屬，設祝冊案於室戶外之右。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites led its subordinates in setting up the prayer-register table to the right outside the chamber doors.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites led its staff in placing the prayer-register table to the right outside the chamber doors.

sentences.zh: 司尊彝帥其屬，設尊彝之位於室戶之左，每位斝彝一、黃彝一、犧尊二、象尊二、著尊二、山罍二，各加勺、冪、坫為酌尊。

translations.literal: The vessel custodian led his subordinates in setting up the positions for ritual vessels to the left of the chamber doors; for each seat one jia yi, one huang yi, two sacrificial zun, two elephant zun, two zhu zun, and two mountain lei, each with ladle, cover, and stand, served as libation vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel custodian led his staff in arranging the ritual vessels to the left of the chamber doors; at each seat were one jia yi, one huang yi, two sacrificial zun, two elephant zun, two zhu zun, and two mountain lei, each fitted with ladle, cover, and stand for libation.

sentences.zh: 又設瓚槃爵坫於篚，置於始祖尊彝所。

translations.literal: Jade cups, trays, wine cups, and stands in baskets were also set up at the place of the Founding Ancestor's ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Jade cups, trays, wine cups, and stands in baskets were also placed at the Founding Ancestor's vessel station.

sentences.zh: 又設壺尊二、太尊二、山罍四，各有坫、冪，在殿下階間，北向西上，設而不酌。

translations.literal: Two hu zun, two tai zun, and four mountain lei were also set up, each with stand and cover, in the space between the steps below the hall, facing north with west as superior; they were displayed but not used for libation.
translations.idiomatic: Two hu zun, two tai zun, and four mountain lei, each with stand and cover, were also placed between the steps below the hall, facing north with the westernmost seat highest in rank; they were displayed but not used for libation.

sentences.zh: 七祀功臣每位設壺尊二于座之左，皆加冪、坫於內，酌尊加勺，皆藉以席。

translations.literal: For the seven sacrifices and merit ministers, two hu zun were set to the left of each seat, all with covers and stands inside; libation vessels had ladles added; all rested on mats.
translations.idiomatic: At each station for the seven sacrifices and merit ministers, two hu zun were placed to the left of the seat, each with cover and stand inside; libation vessels were fitted with ladles, and all rested on mats.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎設祭器，每位四簋在前，四簠次之，次以六醿，次以六鉶，籩豆為後。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman set out the sacrificial vessels: for each seat four gui in front, four fang next, then six yi, then six xing, with baskets and beans last.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman arranged the sacrificial vessels: at each seat four gui in front, four fang next, then six yi, then six xing, with baskets and beans placed last.

sentences.zh: 左十有二籩，右十有二豆，皆濯而陳之，藉以席。

translations.literal: Twelve baskets on the left and twelve beans on the right were all washed and displayed, resting on mats.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve baskets on the left and twelve beans on the right were washed, displayed, and set on mats.

sentences.zh: 籩豆加以巾，蓋於內。

translations.literal: Cloths were placed over the baskets and beans, with covers inside.
translations.idiomatic: Cloths were draped over the baskets and beans, with covers placed beneath them.

sentences.zh: 籩一、豆二、簠一、簋一、並俎四，設於每室饌幔內。

translations.literal: One basket, two beans, one fang, one gui, and four trays together were set inside each chamber's food pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Inside each chamber's food pavilion they placed one basket, two beans, one fang, one gui, and four trays.

sentences.zh: 又設禦洗二於東階之東。

translations.literal: Two imperial hand-washing stations were also set east of the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: Two imperial hand-washing stations were also placed east of the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 又設亞終獻罍洗於東橫街下東南，北向，罍在洗東，篚在洗西，南肆，實以巾。

translations.literal: An urn-washing station for the secondary and final offerers was also set southeast below the eastern cross street, facing north; the urn was east of the basin, the basket west of the basin, displayed facing south and filled with cloths.
translations.idiomatic: An urn-washing station for the secondary and final offerers was also placed southeast below the eastern cross street, facing north—the urn east of the basin, the basket west of the basin, displayed facing south and stocked with cloths.

sentences.zh: 又設亞終獻爵洗於罍洗之西，罍在洗東，篚在洗西，南肆，實以巾、爵並坫。

translations.literal: A cup-washing station for the secondary and final offerers was also set west of the urn-washing station; the urn was east of the basin, the basket west of the basin, displayed facing south and filled with cloths, wine cups, and stands.
translations.idiomatic: A cup-washing station for the secondary and final offerers was also placed west of the urn-washing station—the urn east of the basin, the basket west of the basin, displayed facing south and stocked with cloths, wine cups, and stands.

sentences.zh: 執巾罍巾篚各位於其後。

translations.literal: Officers holding cloths, urn cloths, and baskets each took his position behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Officers holding cloths, urn cloths, and baskets each took his place behind them.

sentences.zh: 享日醜前五刻，太常卿帥執事者，設燭於神位前及戶外。

translations.literal: On the day of offering, five quarters before the hour of chou, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices led the attendants in setting candles before the spirit seats and outside the doors.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of offering, five quarters before the chou hour, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices led the attendants in lighting candles before the spirit seats and outside the doors.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿帥其屬，入實籩豆。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices led his subordinates in filling the baskets and beans.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices led his staff in filling the baskets and beans.

sentences.zh: 籩之實，魚鱐、糗餌、粉餈、乾棗、形鹽、鹿脯、榛實、乾裛、桃、菱、芡、栗，以序為次。

translations.literal: The contents of the baskets were, in order: dried fish, puffed grain and cakes, rice-flour cakes, dried jujubes, shaped salt, venison jerky, hazelnuts, dried meat strips, peaches, water caltrop, gorgon seeds, and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: The baskets were filled, in order, with dried fish, puffed grain and cakes, rice-flour cakes, dried jujubes, shaped salt, venison jerky, hazelnuts, dried meat strips, peaches, water caltrop, gorgon seeds, and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 豆之實，芹菹、筍菹、葵菹、菁菹、韭菹、酏食、魚醢、兔醢、豚拍、鹿臡、醓醢、糝食，以序為次。

translations.literal: The contents of the beans were, in order: pickled celery, pickled bamboo shoots, pickled mallow, pickled turnip greens, pickled leeks, fermented gruel, fish paste, rabbit paste, pork ribs, minced venison, meat paste with seasoning, and mixed grain.
translations.idiomatic: The beans were filled, in order, with pickled celery, pickled bamboo shoots, pickled mallow, pickled turnip greens, pickled leeks, fermented gruel, fish paste, rabbit paste, pork ribs, minced venison, seasoned meat paste, and mixed grain.

sentences.zh: 又鉶實以羹，加芼滑，登實以大羹，簠實以稻粱，簋實以黍稷，粱在稻前，稷在黍前。

translations.literal: The xing vessels were filled with broth and seasoned with greens and meat slices; the deng vessel with great broth; the fang with rice and millet; the gui with panicled millet and glutinous millet—millet before rice, and glutinous millet before panicled millet.
translations.idiomatic: The xing vessels were filled with broth and garnished with greens and meat slices; the deng vessel with great broth; the fang with rice and millet; the gui with panicled millet and glutinous millet—millet placed before rice, and glutinous millet before panicled millet.

sentences.zh: 良醖令入實尊彝。

translations.literal: The Director of Fine Brew entered and filled the ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Fine Brew entered and filled the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 斝彝、黃彝實以鬱鬯，犧尊、象尊、著尊實以玄酒外，皆實以酒用香藥酒，各加坫、勺、冪。

translations.literal: The jia yi and huang yi were filled with fragrant spirit; the sacrificial zun, elephant zun, and zhu zun were filled with dark (unfermented) wine; apart from these, all were filled with spiced medicinal wine, each with stand, ladle, and cover.
translations.idiomatic: The jia yi and huang yi were filled with fragrant spirit; the sacrificial zun, elephant zun, and zhu zun with dark (unfermented) wine; all others with spiced medicinal wine, each fitted with stand, ladle, and cover.

sentences.zh: 殿下之尊罍，壺尊、太尊、山罍，內除山罍上尊實以玄酒外，皆實以酒，加冪、坫。

translations.literal: For the vessels below the hall—the hu zun, tai zun, and mountain lei—apart from the upper mountain lei filled with dark (unfermented) wine, all were filled with wine, with covers and stands added.
translations.idiomatic: For the vessels below the hall—the hu zun, tai zun, and mountain lei—except for the upper mountain lei, which was filled with dark (unfermented) wine, all were filled with wine and fitted with covers and stands.

sentences.zh: 太廟令帥其屬，設七祀功臣席褥于其次，每位各設莞席一、碧綃褥一，又各設版位於其座前，又籩豆簠簋各二、俎一。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his subordinates in setting out mats and cushions for the seven sacrifices and merit ministers at their stations; at each seat one cattail mat and one green silk cushion were set, and at each a tablet position before the seat, with two baskets, two beans, two fang, two gui, and one tray.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his staff in preparing mats and cushions for the seven sacrifices and merit ministers; at each station they placed one cattail mat and one green silk cushion, set a tablet position before the seat, and arranged two baskets, two beans, two fang, two gui, and one tray.

sentences.zh: 每位次各設壺尊二於神座之右，北向，玄酒在西。

translations.literal: At each station two hu zun were set to the right of the spirit seat, facing north, with dark (unfermented) wine on the west.
translations.idiomatic: At each station two hu zun were placed to the right of the spirit seat, facing north, with the dark (unfermented) wine on the west.

sentences.zh: 良醖令以法酒實尊如常，加勺、冪，置爵於尊下，加坫。

translations.literal: The Director of Fine Brew filled the vessels with ceremonial wine as usual, adding ladles and covers, placing wine cups beneath the vessels, and adding stands.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Fine Brew filled the vessels with ceremonial wine as usual, fitted them with ladles and covers, placed wine cups beneath the vessels, and added stands.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿實饌。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices filled the food offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices filled the food offerings.

sentences.zh: 左二籩，栗在前，鹿脯次之。

translations.literal: Two baskets on the left: chestnuts first, venison jerky next.
translations.idiomatic: On the left, two baskets—chestnuts first, venison jerky next.

sentences.zh: 右二豆，菁菹在前，鹿臡次之。

translations.literal: Two beans on the right: pickled turnip greens first, minced venison next.
translations.idiomatic: On the right, two beans—pickled turnip greens first, minced venison next.

sentences.zh: 俎實以羊熟，簠簋實以黍稷。

translations.literal: The tray was filled with cooked mutton; the fang and gui with panicled millet and glutinous millet.
translations.idiomatic: The tray was filled with cooked mutton; the fang and gui with panicled millet and glutinous millet.

sentences.zh: 太廟令又設七祀燎柴，及開瘞坎於西神門外之北。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple also set out firewood for the seven sacrifices' burnt offering and opened the burial pit north of outside the West Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple also prepared firewood for the seven sacrifices' burnt offering and opened the burial pit north of the West Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 太府監陳異寶、嘉瑞、伐國之寶，戶部陳諸州歲貢，金為前列，玉帛次之，餘為後，皆于宮縣之北，東西相向，各藉以席。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Storehouse displayed rare treasures, auspicious omens, and trophies from conquered states; the Ministry of Revenue displayed the annual tribute from the provinces—gold in the front row, silks and jades next, the rest afterward—all north of the court ensemble, facing each other east and west, each resting on a mat.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Storehouse displayed rare treasures, auspicious omens, and trophies from conquered states; the Ministry of Revenue displayed the annual tribute from the provinces—gold in the front row, silks and jades next, everything else afterward—all north of the court ensemble, arranged facing each other east and west, each set on a mat.

sentences.zh: 凡祀神之物，當時所無者則以時物代之。

translations.literal: For all items offered to the spirits, whatever was unavailable at the time was replaced with seasonal substitutes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an item required for offering to the spirits was unavailable, a seasonal substitute was used in its place.

sentences.zh: 省牲器：前一日未後，廟所禁行人。

translations.literal: Inspection of sacrificial animals and vessels: after wei on the preceding day, passage through the temple precinct was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection of sacrificial animals and vessels: after the wei hour on the preceding day, the temple precinct was closed to traffic.

sentences.zh: 司尊彝、奉禮郎及執事者，升自西階以俟。

translations.literal: The vessel custodian, Ritual Gentleman, and attendants ascended by the western steps to await.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel custodian, Ritual Gentleman, and attendants ascended the western steps to await the inspection.

sentences.zh: 少頃，諸太祝與廩犧令，以牲就位。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, all Chief Invokers and the Director of Sacrificial Livestock brought the sacrificial animals into position.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the Chief Invokers and the Director of Sacrificial Livestock brought the sacrificial animals into position.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、贊者引禮部尚書、光祿卿丞詣省牲位，立定。

translations.literal: The ritual officer and announcer led the Minister of Rites and the Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices to the sacrificial inspection station and had them stand in place.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer and announcer escorted the Minister of Rites and the Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices to the sacrificial inspection station and had them take their places.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引禮部尚書，贊引者引御史，入就西階升，遍視滌濯。

translations.literal: The ritual officer led the Minister of Rites; the announcer led the censor. They entered, ascended by the western steps, and inspected all washing and rinsing.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer led the Minister of Rites, and the announcer led the censor; they entered, ascended the western steps, and inspected all the washing and rinsing.

sentences.zh: 訖，執事者皆舉冪曰：「潔。

translations.literal: When finished, all attendants raised the covers and said: "Pure."
translations.idiomatic: When the inspection was finished, all attendants raised the covers and declared, "Pure."

sentences.zh: 」俱降，就省牲位，禮直官稍前曰：「告潔畢，請省牲。

translations.literal: All descended together and took up positions at the sacrificial inspection station; the ritual officer stepped slightly forward and said: "The report of purity is complete. Please inspect the sacrificial animals."
translations.idiomatic: All descended together and took their places at the sacrificial inspection station; the ritual officer stepped forward and said, "The report of purity is complete. Please inspect the sacrificial animals."

sentences.zh: 」次引禮部尚書侍郎稍前，省牲訖，退復位。

translations.literal: Next he led the Minister and Vice Minister of Rites slightly forward; when the inspection of the sacrificial animals was finished, they withdrew and returned to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the Minister and Vice Minister of Rites forward; when the inspection of the sacrificial animals was complete, they withdrew and returned to their positions.

sentences.zh: 次引光祿卿丞出班，巡牲一匝。

translations.literal: Next he led the Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices out of the ranks to circle the sacrificial animals once.
translations.idiomatic: Next he led the Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices out of the ranks to walk once around the sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 光祿丞西向曰：「充。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, facing west, said: "Sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Facing west, the Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices declared, "Sufficient."

translations.literal: He said: "Complete."
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "Complete."

sentences.zh: 」廩犧令帥諸太祝巡牲一匝，西向躬身曰：「腯。

translations.literal: The Director of Sacrificial Livestock led all Chief Invokers in circling the sacrificial animals once; facing west and bowing, he said: "Plump."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Livestock led the Chief Invokers once around the sacrificial animals; facing west and bowing, he declared, "Plump."

sentences.zh: 」禮直官稍前曰：「省牲畢，請就省饌位。

translations.literal: The ritual officer stepped slightly forward and said: "The inspection of the sacrificial animals is complete. Please proceed to the food-inspection station."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer stepped forward and said, "The inspection of the sacrificial animals is complete. Please proceed to the food-inspection station."

sentences.zh: 」引禮部尚書以下各就位，立定。

translations.literal: He led the Minister of Rites and those below him each to his position, where they stood in place.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted the Minister of Rites and his party to their stations, where they took their places.

sentences.zh: 御史省饌具畢，禮直官贊：「省饌訖。

translations.literal: When the censor had finished inspecting the food offerings, the ritual officer announced: "The food inspection is complete."
translations.idiomatic: When the censor had finished inspecting the food offerings, the ritual officer announced, "The food inspection is complete."

sentences.zh: 」俱還齋所。

translations.literal: All returned together to the fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: All returned together to the fasting quarters.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿、丞及太祝、廩犧令以次牽牲詣廚，授太官令。

translations.literal: The Minister and Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, Chief Invokers, and Director of Sacrificial Livestock, in order, led the sacrificial animals to the kitchen and handed them over to the Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In turn, the Minister and Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, the Chief Invokers, and the Director of Sacrificial Livestock led the sacrificial animals to the kitchen and delivered them to the Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引禮部尚書詣廚，省鼎鑊，視濯溉，訖，還齋所。

translations.literal: The ritual officer led the Minister of Rites to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and cooking vessels and to observe the washing and rinsing; when this was done, they returned to the fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer escorted the Minister of Rites to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and cooking vessels and oversee the washing and rinsing; when finished, they returned to the fasting quarters.

sentences.zh: 晡後一刻，太官令帥宰人，執鸞刀割牲，祝史各取毛血，每座共實一豆，遂烹牲。

translations.literal: One quarter-hour after the bibu hour, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led the butchers; wielding the phoenix knife they butchered the sacrificial animals, and each invoker-historian took hair and blood, filling one bean vessel jointly for each seat; then the animals were cooked.
translations.idiomatic: One quarter-hour after the bibu hour, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led the butchers. Wielding the phoenix knife, they slaughtered the sacrificial animals; each invoker-historian collected hair and blood, and for each seat one bean vessel was jointly filled; then the animals were cooked.

sentences.zh: 祝史洗肝于鬱鬯，又取肝惣，每座共實一豆，俱還饌所。

translations.literal: The invoker-historians washed the liver in aromatic fermented millet wine and also took the liver offering; for each seat one bean vessel was jointly filled, and all returned together to the food-preparation station.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker-historians washed the liver in aromatic fermented millet wine and prepared the liver offering; for each seat one bean vessel was jointly filled, then all returned together to the food-preparation station.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕出宮：前一日，有司設大駕鹵簿于應天門外，尚輦進玉輅于應天門內，南向。

translations.literal: The imperial procession leaving the palace: on the preceding day, the responsible officials set out the great parade equipage outside the Gate of Responding to Heaven; the Director of Imperial Chariots brought the jade carriage inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial procession leaving the palace: On the preceding day, the responsible officials deployed the great parade equipage outside the Gate of Responding to Heaven, while the Director of Imperial Chariots brought the jade carriage inside the gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 其日質明，侍臣直衛及導駕官，於致齋殿前，左右分班立俟。

translations.literal: On that day at daybreak, the attending ministers on guard duty and the procession guides, before the Hall of Purification, stood in divided ranks left and right to await.
translations.idiomatic: On that day at daybreak, the attending ministers on guard duty and the procession guides stood in divided ranks to the left and right before the Hall of Purification, awaiting the emperor.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引侍中俯伏，跪，奏：「請中嚴。

translations.literal: A protocol usher led the Palace Attendant forward to prostrate himself, kneel, and report: "Please begin the secondary vigil."
translations.idiomatic: A protocol usher led the Palace Attendant forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported, "Please begin the secondary vigil."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍。

translations.literal: The emperor donned the Through-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put on the Through-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 少頃，侍中奏：「外辦。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, the Palace Attendant reported: "External preparations are complete."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the Palace Attendant reported, "External preparations are complete."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝出齋室，即御座，群官起居訖，尚輦進輿。

translations.literal: The emperor left the fasting chamber, took the imperial seat; when the officials' salutation was finished, the Director of Imperial Chariots brought forward the sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the fasting chamber and took the imperial seat. When the officials had finished their salutation, the Director of Imperial Chariots brought forward the sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏：「請皇帝升輿。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported: "Please let the emperor ascend the sedan."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported, "Please let the emperor ascend the sedan chair."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝乘輿，侍衛警蹕如常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the sedan; guards cleared the way according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the sedan chair, and the guards cleared the way according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 太僕卿先詣玉輅所，攝衣而升，正立執轡。
