translations.literal: The Minister of the Imperial Stud first went to the jade carriage, gathered his robes, mounted, stood upright, and held the reins.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Imperial Stud went first to the jade carriage, gathered his robes, mounted, stood upright, and held the reins.

sentences.zh: 導駕官前導，皇帝至應天門內玉輅所，侍中進當輿前，奏：「請皇帝降輿升輅。

translations.literal: The procession guides led the way; when the emperor reached the jade carriage inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven, the Palace Attendant stepped forward before the sedan and reported: "Please let the emperor descend from the sedan and mount the carriage."
translations.idiomatic: The procession guides led the way. When the emperor reached the jade carriage inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven, the Palace Attendant stepped forward before the sedan and reported, "Please let the emperor descend from the sedan and mount the carriage."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝升輅。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the carriage.

sentences.zh: 太僕卿立授綏，導駕官分左右步導，以裏為上。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Imperial Stud, standing, presented the hand rope; the procession guides walked in front to left and right, taking the inner side as the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Standing in place, the Minister of the Imperial Stud presented the hand rope; the procession guides walked ahead to left and right, keeping to the inner side as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎進當輅前，奏：「請車駕進發。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Chancellery stepped forward before the carriage and reported: "Please let the imperial procession depart."
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Chancellery stepped forward before the carriage and reported, "Please let the imperial procession depart."

sentences.zh: 」奏訖，俯伏，興，退復位。

translations.literal: When the report was finished, he prostrated himself, rose, withdrew, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished his report, he prostrated himself, rose, withdrew, and returned to his position.

sentences.zh: 侍衛儀物止于應天門內，車駕動，稱：「警蹕。

translations.literal: The guard ceremonial objects halted inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven; when the procession moved, the cry was made: "Clear the way!"
translations.idiomatic: The guard ceremonial objects stopped inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven. When the procession moved, the call rang out, "Clear the way!"

sentences.zh: 」至應天門，門下侍郎奏：「請車駕少駐，敕侍臣上馬。

translations.literal: At the Gate of Responding to Heaven, the Vice Director of the Chancellery reported: "Please let the imperial procession pause briefly and decree that the attending ministers mount their horses."
translations.idiomatic: At the Gate of Responding to Heaven, the Vice Director of the Chancellery reported, "Please let the imperial procession pause briefly and decree that the attending ministers mount their horses."

sentences.zh: 」侍中奉旨退，稱曰：「制可。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant received the decree and withdrew, announcing: "The decree is approved."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant received the decree and withdrew, announcing, "The decree is approved."

sentences.zh: 」門下侍郎退，傳制，稱：「侍臣上馬。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Chancellery withdrew, transmitted the decree, and announced: "Let the attending ministers mount their horses."
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Chancellery withdrew, transmitted the decree, and announced, "Let the attending ministers mount their horses."

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳：「敕侍臣上馬。

translations.literal: The announcer received and relayed the transmission: "By decree, let the attending ministers mount their horses."
translations.idiomatic: The announcer received the transmission and relayed, "By decree, let the attending ministers mount their horses."

sentences.zh: 」導駕官分左右前導，門下侍郎奏：「請車駕進發。

translations.literal: The procession guides led the way to left and right; the Vice Director of the Chancellery reported: "Please let the imperial procession depart."
translations.idiomatic: The procession guides led the way to left and right. The Vice Director of the Chancellery reported, "Please let the imperial procession depart."

sentences.zh: 」車駕動，稱「警蹕」，不鳴鼓吹。

translations.literal: The procession moved; the cry "Clear the way!" was made, but drums and wind instruments were not sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The procession moved. The call "Clear the way!" rang out, but drums and wind instruments were not sounded.

sentences.zh: 將至太廟，禮直官、贊者各引享官，通事舍人分引從享群官、宗室子孫，於廟門外，立班奉迎。

translations.literal: As they neared the Grand Ancestral Temple, ritual officers and announcers each led the sacrifice officiants; protocol ushers separately led the assisting civil and military officials and imperial clansmen and descendants; outside the temple gate they formed ranks to welcome the procession.
translations.idiomatic: As they approached the Grand Ancestral Temple, ritual officers and announcers each escorted the sacrifice officiants, while protocol ushers separately led the assisting civil and military officials and imperial clansmen and descendants; outside the temple gate they formed ranks to welcome the emperor.

sentences.zh: 駕至廟門，回輅南向，侍中於輅前奏稱：「侍中臣某言，請皇帝降輅，步入廟門。

translations.literal: When the procession reached the temple gate, the carriage was turned to face south; before the carriage the Palace Attendant reported: "Your subject the Palace Attendant so-and-so reports: Please let the emperor descend from the carriage and enter the temple gate on foot."
translations.idiomatic: When the procession reached the temple gate, the carriage was turned to face south. Before the carriage the Palace Attendant reported, "Your subject the Palace Attendant so-and-so reports: Please let the emperor descend from the carriage and enter the temple gate on foot."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝降輅，導駕官前導，皇帝步入廟門，稍東。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the carriage; the procession guides led the way, and the emperor walked into the temple gate, slightly to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended from the carriage. The procession guides led the way as the emperor walked through the temple gate, bearing slightly east.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏：「請皇帝升輿。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported: "Please let the emperor ascend the sedan."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported, "Please let the emperor ascend the sedan chair."

sentences.zh: 」尚輦奉輿，侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Chariots presented the sedan; guards attended according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Chariots presented the sedan chair, and the guards attended according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輿至大次，侍中奏：「請皇帝降輿，入就大次。

translations.literal: The emperor rode the sedan to the grand rest pavilion; the Palace Attendant reported: "Please let the emperor descend from the sedan and enter the grand rest pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode the sedan chair to the grand rest pavilion. The Palace Attendant reported, "Please let the emperor descend from the sedan and enter the grand rest pavilion."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝入就次，簾降，傘扇侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor entered and took his place in the pavilion; the curtains were lowered; umbrellas, fans, and guards attended according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered and took his place in the pavilion. The curtains were lowered, and umbrellas, fans, and guards attended according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、太常博士各分立于大次左右。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music and the academicians of the Ministry of Ritual Music each stood in divided ranks to the left and right of the grand rest pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music and the academicians of the Ministry of Ritual Music stood in divided ranks to the left and right of the grand rest pavilion.

sentences.zh: 導駕官詣廟庭班位，立俟。

translations.literal: The procession guides went to their ranks in the temple courtyard and stood to await.
translations.idiomatic: The procession guides went to their assigned ranks in the temple courtyard and stood awaiting the rites.

sentences.zh: 晨稞：享日醜前五刻，諸享官及助祭官，各服其服。

translations.literal: Morning libation: on the day of the sacrifice, five quarter-hours before the chou hour, all sacrifice officiants and assisting sacrifice officials each donned their prescribed robes.
translations.idiomatic: Morning libation: On the day of the sacrifice, five quarter-hours before the chou hour, all sacrifice officiants and assisting sacrifice officials donned their prescribed robes.

sentences.zh: 太廟令、良醖令帥其屬，入實尊罍。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple and the Director of Fine Brew led their subordinates to fill the zun and lei vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple and the Director of Fine Brew led their staffs to fill the zun and lei vessels.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿、太官令、進饌者實籩豆簠簋，並徹去蓋冪。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen, and those who brought forward the food offerings filled the baskets, beans, fang, and gui, and removed all covers.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen, and those bearing the food offerings filled the baskets, beans, fang, and gui and removed all covers.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎、贊者先入，就位。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman and announcers entered first and took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman and the announcers entered first and took their positions.

sentences.zh: 贊者引御史、太廟令、太祝、宮闈令、祝史與執事官等，各自東偏門入，就位。

translations.literal: Announcers led the censor, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, Chief Invokers, Director of the Palace Enclosure, invoker-historians, and attending officials, each entering by the east side gate and taking his position.
translations.idiomatic: Announcers led the censor, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, the Chief Invokers, the Director of the Palace Enclosure, the invoker-historians, and the attending officials, each entering through the east side gate and taking his position.

sentences.zh: 未明二刻，禮直官引太常寺官屬並太祝、宮闈令升殿，開始祖祏室。

translations.literal: Two quarter-hours before dawn, ritual officers led the officials of the Ministry of Ritual Music together with the Chief Invokers and Director of the Palace Enclosure up to the hall, opened the founding ancestor's spirit-tablet chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Two quarter-hours before dawn, ritual officers led the officials of the Ministry of Ritual Music, the Chief Invokers, and the Director of the Palace Enclosure up to the hall and opened the founding ancestor's spirit-tablet chamber.

sentences.zh: 太祝、宮闈令捧出帝后神主，設於座。

translations.literal: The Chief Invokers and Director of the Palace Enclosure carried out the spirit tablets of the emperor and empress and set them on their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invokers and the Director of the Palace Enclosure carried out the spirit tablets of the emperor and empress and set them on their seats.

sentences.zh: 以次，逐室神主各設於內黼扆前，置定。

translations.literal: In order, the spirit tablets of each chamber were each set before the inner embroidered screen and fixed in place.
translations.idiomatic: In turn, the spirit tablets from each chamber were placed before the inner embroidered screen and set in position.

sentences.zh: 贊者引御史、太廟令、宮闈令、太祝、祝史與太常官屬，於當階間，重行北向立。

translations.literal: Announcers led the censor, Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, Director of the Palace Enclosure, Chief Invokers, invoker-historians, and officials of the Ministry of Ritual Music to stand in double rows facing north between the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Announcers led the censor, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, the Director of the Palace Enclosure, the Chief Invokers, the invoker-historians, and the officials of the Ministry of Ritual Music to stand in double rows facing north between the steps.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎於殿上贊：「奉神主。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman on the hall announced: "Present the spirit tablets."
translations.idiomatic: On the hall the Ritual Gentleman announced, "Present the spirit tablets."

sentences.zh: 」訖，奉禮曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: When this was finished, the Ritual Gentleman said: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, the Ritual Gentleman said, "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，御史以下皆再拜，訖，各就位。

translations.literal: The announcers received and relayed the announcement; the censor and all below bowed twice; when finished, each returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The announcers relayed the command. The censor and all ranks below bowed twice; when finished, each returned to his position.

sentences.zh: 大樂令帥工人二舞入。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Music led the musicians of the two dances to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Grand Music led the musicians of the two dances to enter.

sentences.zh: 就位。

translations.literal: They took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: They took their positions.

sentences.zh: 禮直官贊者各引享官，通事舍人分引助祭文武群官宗室入就位。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and announcers each led the sacrifice officiants; protocol ushers separately led assisting civil and military officials and clansmen of the imperial house to enter and take their positions.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and announcers each escorted the sacrifice officiants, while protocol ushers separately led the assisting civil and military officials and clansmen of the imperial house to enter and take their positions.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶，陳于宮縣之北。

translations.literal: The seal and regalia officer presented the imperial treasures and displayed them north of the court ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: The seal and regalia officer presented the imperial treasures and displayed them north of the court ensemble.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入大次。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the grand rest pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the grand rest pavilion.

sentences.zh: 少頃，侍中奏：「請中嚴。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, the Palace Attendant reported: "Please begin the secondary vigil."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the Palace Attendant reported, "Please begin the secondary vigil."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝服袞冕。

translations.literal: The emperor donned the ceremonial robe and crown.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put on the ceremonial robe and crown.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏：「外辦。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported: "External preparations are complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported, "External preparations are complete."

sentences.zh: 」太常卿俯伏，跪，奏稱：「太常卿臣某言，請皇帝行事。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Your subject the Minister of Ritual Music so-and-so reports: Please let the emperor perform the rites."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music prostrated himself, knelt, and reported, "Your subject the Minister of Ritual Music so-and-so reports: Please let the emperor perform the rites."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself and rose.

sentences.zh: 簾卷，皇帝出次。

translations.literal: The curtains were raised; the emperor left the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The curtains were raised, and the emperor left the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、太常博士前導，傘扇侍衛如常儀，大禮使後從。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music and the academicians of the Ministry of Ritual Music led the way; umbrellas, fans, and guards attended according to the usual protocol; the Grand Ritual Envoy followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music and the academicians of the Ministry of Ritual Music led the way, with umbrellas, fans, and guards attending according to the usual protocol, while the Grand Ritual Envoy followed behind.

sentences.zh: 至東神門外，殿中監跪進鎮圭，太常卿奏：「請執圭。

translations.literal: At the outside of the East Spirit Gate, the Director of the Palace Directorate knelt and presented the scepter of authority; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the scepter."
translations.idiomatic: Outside the East Spirit Gate, the Director of the Palace Directorate knelt and presented the scepter of authority. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the scepter."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝執鎮圭。

translations.literal: The emperor took the scepter of authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the scepter of authority.

sentences.zh: 傘扇仗衛停於門外，近侍者從入。

translations.literal: Umbrellas, fans, and armed guards halted outside the gate; close attendants followed inside.
translations.idiomatic: Umbrellas, fans, and armed guards stopped outside the gate, while close attendants followed the emperor inside.

sentences.zh: 協律郎跪伏舉麾，興。

translations.literal: The pitch-master knelt, prostrated himself, raised the banner, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-master knelt, prostrated himself, raised the banner, and rose.

sentences.zh: 工鼓柷，宮縣《昌甯之樂》作。

translations.literal: The musicians struck the zhu; the court ensemble performed the music "Changning."
translations.idiomatic: The musicians struck the zhu, and the court ensemble performed the music "Changning."

sentences.zh: 至阼階下，偃麾，戛敔，樂止。

translations.literal: At the foot of the east steps, the banner was lowered, the yu was tapped, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the east steps, the banner was lowered, the yu was tapped, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 升自阼階，登歌樂作，左右侍從量人數升至版位，西向立，樂止。

translations.literal: Ascending by the east steps, the elevated choir music began; attendants to left and right, according to their number, ascended to the throne position and stood facing west; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending by the east steps to the elevated choir music, attendants to left and right ascended in number to the throne position and stood facing west; then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 前導官分左右侍立。

translations.literal: The leading guides stood in attendance to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The leading guides stood in attendance to left and right.

sentences.zh: 太常卿前奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music stepped forward and reported: "Please bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music stepped forward and reported, "Please bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰：「眾官再拜。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman said: "Let all officials bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman said, "Let all officials bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，凡在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The announcers received and relayed the announcement; all who stood in their positions bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The announcers relayed the command, and all who stood in their positions bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 奉禮又贊：「諸執事者各就位。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman again announced: "Let all attending officials take their positions."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman announced again, "Let all attending officials take their positions."

sentences.zh: 」禮直官、贊者分引執事者各就殿上下之位。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and announcers separately led the attending officials each to his position above and below in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and announcers separately escorted the attending officials each to his assigned position above and below in the hall.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請皇帝詣罍洗位。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please let the emperor proceed to the vessel-washing station."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please let the emperor proceed to the vessel-washing station."

sentences.zh: 」登歌樂作，至阼階，樂止。

translations.literal: The elevated choir music began; at the east steps, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The elevated choir music began; when he reached the east steps, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 降自阼階，宮縣樂作，至洗位，樂止。

translations.literal: Descending by the east steps, the court ensemble music began; at the washing station, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Descending by the east steps to the court ensemble music, he reached the washing station and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 內侍跪取匜，興，沃水。

translations.literal: A palace attendant knelt, took the pitcher, rose, and poured water.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant knelt, took the pitcher, rose, and poured water.

sentences.zh: 又內侍跪取槃，興，承水。

translations.literal: Another palace attendant knelt, took the basin, rose, and received the water.
translations.idiomatic: Another palace attendant knelt, took the basin, rose, and received the water.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請搢鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please tuck the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please tuck the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝搢鎮圭，盥手，訖，內侍跪取巾於篚，興，以進。

translations.literal: The emperor tucked the scepter of authority and washed his hands; when finished, a palace attendant knelt, took a cloth from the basket, rose, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tucked the scepter of authority and washed his hands. When finished, a palace attendant knelt, took a cloth from the basket, rose, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帨手，訖。

translations.literal: He dried his hands; when finished.
translations.idiomatic: He dried his hands.

sentences.zh: 奉瓚官以瓚跪進，皇帝受瓚，內侍奉匜，沃水，又內侍跪奉槃承水，洗瓚訖。

translations.literal: The libation-cup bearer knelt and presented the jade libation cup; the emperor received the cup; a palace attendant presented the pitcher and poured water; another palace attendant knelt and presented the basin to receive the water; the cup was washed; when finished.
translations.idiomatic: The libation-cup bearer knelt and presented the jade libation cup. The emperor received the cup; a palace attendant presented the pitcher and poured water, while another palace attendant knelt and held the basin to receive the water until the washing was complete.

sentences.zh: 內侍跪奉巾以進，皇帝拭瓚，訖，內侍奠槃匜，又奠巾於篚。

translations.literal: A palace attendant knelt and presented a cloth; the emperor wiped the cup; when finished, the palace attendant set down the basin and pitcher, and also set the cloth in the basket.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant knelt and presented a cloth. The emperor wiped the cup clean; when finished, the attendant set down the basin and pitcher and placed the cloth back in the basket.

sentences.zh: 奉瓚槃官以槃受瓚。

translations.literal: The libation-cup tray bearer received the cup with the tray.
translations.idiomatic: The libation-cup tray bearer received the cup on the tray.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請執鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」前導，皇帝升殿，宮縣樂作，至阼階下，樂止。

translations.literal: Leading the way, the emperor ascended the hall; the court ensemble music began; at the foot of the east steps, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With the guides leading the way, the emperor ascended the hall to the court ensemble music; at the foot of the east steps the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升自阼階，登歌樂作，太常卿前導，詣始祖位酌尊所，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended by the east steps; the elevated choir music began; the Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the founding ancestor's station where the zun was poured; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended by the east steps to the elevated choir music. The Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the founding ancestor's station at the wine-pouring place, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 奉瓚槃官以瓚蒞鬯，執尊者舉冪，侍中跪酌鬱鬯，訖，太常卿前導，入詣始祖室神位前，北向立。

translations.literal: The libation-cup tray bearer drew aromatic fermented millet wine into the cup; the bearer of the zun raised the cover; the Palace Attendant knelt and poured the aromatic wine; when finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way inward to before the spirit seat of the founding ancestor's chamber and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The libation-cup tray bearer drew aromatic fermented millet wine into the cup. The bearer of the zun raised its cover, and the Palace Attendant knelt to pour the aromatic wine. When finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way inward to before the spirit seat in the founding ancestor's chamber, and they stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請搢鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please tuck the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please tuck the scepter of authority."

translations.literal: He knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knelt.

sentences.zh: 奉瓚槃官西向跪，以瓚授奉瓚官，奉瓚西向以瓚跪進。

translations.literal: The libation-cup tray bearer, kneeling and facing west, handed the cup to the libation-cup bearer; the libation-cup bearer, facing west, knelt and presented the cup.
translations.idiomatic: The libation-cup tray bearer knelt facing west and handed the cup to the libation-cup bearer, who knelt facing west and presented the cup.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請執瓚以鬯稞地。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take the cup and pour the aromatic wine as a ground libation."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take the cup and pour the aromatic wine as a ground libation."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝執瓚以鬯稞地，訖，以瓚授奉瓚槃官，太常卿奏：「請執鎮圭。

translations.literal: The emperor took the cup and poured the aromatic wine as a ground libation; when finished, he handed the cup to the libation-cup tray bearer; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the cup and poured the aromatic wine as a ground libation. When finished, he handed the cup to the libation-cup tray bearer. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興，前導出戶外。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself, rose, and was led forward out through the doorway.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, rose, and was led forward out through the doorway.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝再拜，太常卿前導詣次位，並如上儀。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice; the Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the next position, all according to the procedure above.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice. The Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the next position, all according to the procedure described above.

sentences.zh: 祼畢。

translations.literal: The libation was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The libation rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請還版位。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please return to the throne position."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please return to the throne position."

sentences.zh: 」登歌樂作，至版位西向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The elevated choir music began; he reached the throne position and stood facing west; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: To the elevated choir music, he returned to the throne position and stood facing west; then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請還小次。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please return to the minor rest pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please return to the minor rest pavilion."

sentences.zh: 」前導皇帝行，登歌樂作，降自阼階，登歌樂止，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: Leading the emperor forward, the guides proceeded; the elevated choir music began; descending by the east steps, the elevated choir music stopped and the court ensemble music began.
translations.idiomatic: With the guides leading the emperor forward, the elevated choir music began. Descending by the east steps, the elevated choir music stopped and the court ensemble music began.

sentences.zh: 將至小次，太常卿奏：「請釋鎮圭。

translations.literal: As they neared the minor rest pavilion, the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please release the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: As they approached the minor rest pavilion, the Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please release the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」殿中監跪受鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and received the scepter of authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt to receive the scepter of authority.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入小次，簾降，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the minor rest pavilion; the screen was lowered, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the minor rest pavilion. The screen was lowered and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 少頃，宮縣奏《來甯之曲》，以黃鍾為宮，大呂為角，大簇為徵，應鍾為羽，作《仁豐道洽之舞》，九成止。

translations.literal: After a short while, the court ensemble performed the melody "Laining," with huangzhong as gong, dalü as jue, dacui as zhi, and yingzhong as yu; they performed the dance "Benevolence Abundant, the Way in Harmony," and stopped after nine movements.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the court ensemble performed the melody "Laining," using huangzhong as gong, dalü as jue, dacui as zhi, and yingzhong as yu, and danced "Benevolence Abundant, the Way in Harmony" through nine movements before stopping.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘三奏，大呂、太簇、應鐘各再奏，送神通用《來甯之曲》。

translations.literal: Huangzhong was played three times; dalü, dacui, and yingzhong were each played twice; for sending off the spirits the melody "Laining" was used in general.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was played three times, dalü, dacui, and yingzhong were each played twice, and the melody "Laining" was used generally for sending off the spirits.

sentences.zh: 初，晨稞將畢，祝史各奉毛血及肝惣之豆，先于南神門外，齋郎奉爐炭蕭蒿黍稷，各立於肝惣之後。

translations.literal: At the beginning, as the morning libation was nearing completion, each invoker-historian bore the bean vessels of hair and blood and of the liver offering and waited first outside the south spirit gate; offering-attendants bore brazier coals, artemisia, and millet, each standing behind the liver offering.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the morning libation was nearing completion, each invoker-historian carried the bean vessels of hair and blood and of the liver offering and waited outside the south spirit gate. Offering-attendants carried brazier coals, artemisia, and millet, each standing behind the liver offering.

sentences.zh: 皇帝既晨稞畢，至樂作六成，皆入自正門，升自太階。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had finished the morning libation, when the music reached its sixth movement, all entered by the main gate and ascended by the grand steps.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had completed the morning libation, and when the music reached its sixth movement, all entered through the main gate and ascended the grand steps.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝於階上各迎毛血肝稞，進奠於神座前。

translations.literal: All the Chief Invokers, on the steps, each received the hair and blood and liver libation and advanced to set them before the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: On the steps, each of the Chief Invokers received the hair and blood and liver libation and carried them forward to set them before the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 祝史立於尊所，齋郎奉爐置於室戶外之左，其蕭蒿黍稷各置於爐炭下。

translations.literal: The invoker-historians stood at the ritual vessel station; offering-attendants bore the brazier and set it to the left outside the chamber door, and the artemisia and millet were each placed beneath the brazier coals.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker-historians stood at the ritual vessel station. Offering-attendants brought the brazier and placed it to the left outside the chamber door, with the artemisia and millet set beneath the brazier coals.

sentences.zh: 齋郎降自西階，諸太祝各取肝燔於爐，還尊所。

translations.literal: The offering-attendants descended by the west steps; each Chief Invoker took the liver and burned it on the brazier, then returned to the ritual vessel station.
translations.idiomatic: The offering-attendants descended the west steps. Each Chief Invoker took the liver and burned it on the brazier, then returned to the ritual vessel station.

sentences.zh: 進熟：皇帝升稞，太官令帥進饌者，奉陳于南神門外諸饌幔內，以西為上。

translations.literal: Presenting cooked offerings: the emperor ascended for the libation; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led those bringing forward the food offerings and had them displayed within the food-offering pavilions outside the south spirit gate, with west taking precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting cooked offerings: as the emperor ascended for the libation, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led those bearing the food offerings and had them arranged within the food-offering pavilions outside the south spirit gate, with the westernmost position highest in rank.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒出詣饌所，與薦俎齋郎奉俎，並薦籩豆簠簋官奉籩豆簠簋，禮直官、太官令引以序入自正門，宮縣《豐甯之樂》作。

translations.literal: The ritual officer led the Minister over the Masses out to the food-preparation station; together with the tray-presenting offering-attendants bearing the trays, and the officers presenting baskets, beans, fang, and gui bearing baskets, beans, fang, and gui, the ritual officer and Director of the Imperial Kitchen led them in order through the main gate; the court ensemble performed the music "Fengning."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer escorted the Minister over the Masses to the food-preparation station. Together with the tray-presenting offering-attendants bearing the trays and the officers presenting baskets, beans, fang, and gui, the ritual officer and Director of the Imperial Kitchen led them in order through the main gate as the court ensemble performed the music "Fengning."

sentences.zh: 徹豆通用。

translations.literal: Removal of the bean vessels follows the general procedure.
translations.idiomatic: The removal of bean vessels follows the standard procedure.

sentences.zh: 至太階，樂止。

translations.literal: At the grand steps, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand steps, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 祝史俱進徹毛血之豆，降自西階，以出。

translations.literal: The invoker-historians together advanced and removed the bean vessels of hair and blood, descended by the west steps, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker-historians together advanced to remove the bean vessels of hair and blood, then descended the west steps and departed.

sentences.zh: 饌升，諸太祝迎於階上，各設於神位前。

translations.literal: The food offerings were brought up; all the Chief Invokers received them on the steps and each set them before a spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: The food offerings were brought up. On the steps, the Chief Invokers received them and each set them before a spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 先薦牛，次薦羊，次薦豕及魚。

translations.literal: The ox was presented first, then the sheep, then the pig and fish.
translations.idiomatic: The ox was presented first, then the sheep, then the pig and fish.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒以下，降自西階，復位。

translations.literal: The ritual officer led the Minister over the Masses and those below him down by the west steps, and they returned to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer led the Minister over the Masses and those below him down the west steps, and they returned to their positions.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝各取蕭蒿黍稷擩於脂，燎於爐炭，訖，還尊所。

translations.literal: Each Chief Invoker took artemisia and millet, dipped them in fat, and burned them on the brazier coals; when finished, they returned to the ritual vessel station.
translations.idiomatic: Each Chief Invoker took artemisia and millet, dipped them in fat, and burned them on the brazier coals. When finished, they returned to the ritual vessel station.

sentences.zh: 贊者引舉冊官升自西階，詣始祖位之右，進取祝冊置在版位之西，置訖，于祝冊案近南立。

translations.literal: An announcer led the register bearer up by the west steps to the right of the founding ancestor's seat; he advanced, took the prayer register, and placed it west of the throne position; when this was done, he stood near the south side of the prayer-register table.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer led the register bearer up the west steps to the right of the founding ancestor's seat. He advanced, took the prayer register, and placed it west of the throne position, then stood near the south side of the prayer-register table.

sentences.zh: 太常卿跪奏：「請詣罍洗位。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music knelt and reported: "Please proceed to the urn-washing station."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music knelt and reported, "Please proceed to the urn-washing station."

sentences.zh: 」簾卷，出次，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The screen was raised; he left the pavilion; the court ensemble music began.
translations.idiomatic: The screen was raised. He left the pavilion, and the court ensemble music began.

sentences.zh: 殿中監跪進鎮圭，太常卿奏：「請執鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and presented the scepter of authority; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and presented the scepter of authority. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」前導，詣罍洗位，樂止。

translations.literal: Led forward, he proceeded to the urn-washing station; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Led forward, he proceeded to the urn-washing station, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 盥手，洗爵，並如晨稞之儀。

translations.literal: He washed his hands and washed the cup, all according to the procedure for the morning libation.
translations.idiomatic: He washed his hands and washed the cup, all according to the morning libation procedure.

sentences.zh: 盥洗訖，太常卿奏：「請執鎮圭。

translations.literal: When the washing was finished, the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: When the washing was finished, the Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」前導，升殿，宮縣樂作，至阼階下，樂止。

translations.literal: Led forward, he ascended the hall; the court ensemble music began; at the foot of the east steps, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Led forward, he ascended the hall to the court ensemble music. At the foot of the east steps, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 升自阼階，登歌樂作。

translations.literal: He ascended by the east steps; the elevated choir music began.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the east steps as the elevated choir music began.

sentences.zh: 太常卿前導，詣始祖位尊彝所，登歌樂作，至尊彝所，登歌樂止，宮縣奏《大元之樂》，文舞進。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the zun and yi vessel station at the founding ancestor's seat; the elevated choir music began; upon reaching the zun and yi station, the elevated choir music stopped; the court ensemble performed the music "Dayuan," and the civil dancers advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the zun and yi vessel station at the founding ancestor's seat. The elevated choir music began, then stopped upon reaching the station. The court ensemble performed the music "Dayuan," and the civil dancers advanced.

sentences.zh: 奉爵官以爵蒞尊，執尊者舉冪，侍中跪酌犧尊之泛齊，訖，太常卿前導，入詣始祖室神位前，北向立。

translations.literal: The wine-cup bearer drew wine from the zun into the cup; the bearer of the zun raised the cover; the Palace Attendant knelt and poured the first-stage fermented wine from the sacrificial zun; when finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way inward to before the spirit seat in the founding ancestor's chamber, and they stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The wine-cup bearer drew wine from the zun into the cup. The bearer of the zun raised its cover, and the Palace Attendant knelt to pour the first-stage fermented wine from the sacrificial zun. When finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way inward to before the spirit seat in the founding ancestor's chamber, and they stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請搢鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please tuck in the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please tuck in the scepter of authority."

translations.literal: He knelt.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt.

sentences.zh: 奉爵官以爵授進爵酒官。

translations.literal: The wine-cup bearer handed the cup to the wine-presenting officer.
translations.idiomatic: The wine-cup bearer handed the cup to the wine-presenting officer.

sentences.zh: 進爵酒官西向以爵跪進，太常卿奏：「請執爵三祭酒。

translations.literal: The wine-presenting officer, facing west, knelt and presented the cup; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take the cup and pour three libations."
translations.idiomatic: The wine-presenting officer knelt facing west and presented the cup. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take the cup and pour three libations."

sentences.zh: 」三祭酒于茅苴，訖，以爵授進爵酒官，進爵酒官以爵授奉爵官。

translations.literal: He poured three libations onto the thatched bundle; when finished, he handed the cup to the wine-presenting officer, and the wine-presenting officer handed the cup to the wine-cup bearer.
translations.idiomatic: He poured three libations onto the thatched bundle. When finished, he handed the cup to the wine-presenting officer, who in turn handed it to the wine-cup bearer.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請執鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the scepter of authority."

translations.literal: He rose.
translations.idiomatic: He rose.

sentences.zh: 前導，出戶外，太常卿奏：「請少立。

translations.literal: Led forward, he went out through the doorway; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please stand briefly."
translations.idiomatic: Led forward, he went out through the doorway. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please stand briefly."

sentences.zh: 」樂止。

translations.literal: The music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased.

sentences.zh: 舉冊官進舉祝冊，中書侍郎搢笏跪讀祝，舉祝官舉冊奠訖，先詣次位。

translations.literal: The register bearer advanced and raised the prayer register; the Vice Director of the Secretariat tucked in his tablet, knelt, and read the prayer; the prayer-elevating officer raised the register and set it down; when finished, he proceeded first to the next position.
translations.idiomatic: The register bearer advanced and raised the prayer register. The Vice Director of the Secretariat tucked in his tablet, knelt, and read the prayer. The prayer-elevating officer raised the register and set it down, then proceeded first to the next position.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」再拜訖，太常卿前導，詣次位行禮，並如上儀。

translations.literal: When the double bow was finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way and proceeded to the next position to perform the rites, all according to the procedure above.
translations.idiomatic: When the double bow was finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way to the next position to perform the rites, all according to the procedure described above.

sentences.zh: 酌獻畢，太常卿前導還版位，登歌樂作，至位西向立定，樂止。

translations.literal: When the libation presentation was finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way back to the throne position; the elevated choir music began; upon reaching the position he stood facing west; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the libation presentation was finished, the Minister of Ritual Music led the way back to the throne position. The elevated choir music began, and upon reaching the position he stood facing west before the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請還小次。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please return to the minor rest pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please return to the minor rest pavilion."

sentences.zh: 」登歌樂作，降自阼階，登歌樂止，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The elevated choir music began; he descended by the east steps; the elevated choir music stopped, and the court ensemble music began.
translations.idiomatic: The elevated choir music began. Descending the east steps, the elevated choir music stopped and the court ensemble music began.

sentences.zh: 將至小次，太常卿奏：「請釋鎮圭。

translations.literal: As they neared the minor rest pavilion, the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please release the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: As they approached the minor rest pavilion, the Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please release the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」殿中監跪受鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and received the scepter of authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt to receive the scepter of authority.

sentences.zh: 入小次，簾降，樂止，文舞退，武舞進，宮縣奏《肅甯之樂》，作《功成治定之舞》，舞者立定，樂止。

translations.literal: He entered the minor rest pavilion; the screen was lowered; the music stopped; the civil dancers withdrew and the military dancers advanced; the court ensemble performed the music "Suning" and the dance "Merit Achieved, Order Established"; the dancers stood in place; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the minor rest pavilion. The screen was lowered and the music ceased. The civil dancers withdrew and the military dancers advanced. The court ensemble performed the music "Suning" and the dance "Merit Achieved, Order Established." The dancers stood in place, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 皇帝酌獻訖，將詣小次，禮直官引博士，博士引亞獻，詣盥洗位，北向立，搢圭，盥手，帨手，執圭。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished the libation presentation and was about to proceed to the minor rest pavilion, the ritual officer led the academicians; the academicians led the secondary offerer to the hand-washing station; he stood facing north, tucked in his tablet, washed his hands, dried his hands, and took up the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had finished the libation presentation and was about to proceed to the minor rest pavilion, the ritual officer led the academicians, and the academicians led the secondary offerer to the hand-washing station. He stood facing north, tucked in his tablet, washed and dried his hands, and took up the tablet.

sentences.zh: 詣爵洗位，北向立，搢圭，洗爵、拭爵以授執事者，執圭。

translations.literal: He proceeded to the cup-washing station, stood facing north, tucked in his tablet, washed and wiped the cup and handed it to an attendant, then took up the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to the cup-washing station and stood facing north. He tucked in his tablet, washed and wiped the cup, handed it to an attendant, and took up the tablet again.

sentences.zh: 升自西階，詣始祖位尊彝所，西向立。

translations.literal: He ascended by the west steps and proceeded to the zun and yi vessel station at the founding ancestor's seat, standing facing west.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the west steps and proceeded to the zun and yi vessel station at the founding ancestor's seat, where he stood facing west.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The court ensemble music began.
translations.idiomatic: The court ensemble music began.

sentences.zh: 執事者以爵授亞獻，亞獻搢圭，執爵，執尊者舉冪，太官令酌象尊之醴齊，訖，詣始祖神位前，搢圭，跪。

translations.literal: An attendant handed the cup to the secondary offerer; the secondary offerer tucked in his tablet and took the cup; the bearer of the zun raised the cover; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen poured the mild fermented wine from the elephant zun; when finished, he proceeded before the founding ancestor's spirit seat, tucked in his tablet, and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant handed the cup to the secondary offerer. He tucked in his tablet and took the cup. The bearer of the zun raised its cover, and the Director of the Imperial Kitchen poured the mild fermented wine from the elephant zun. When finished, he proceeded before the founding ancestor's spirit seat, tucked in his tablet, and knelt.

sentences.zh: 執事者以爵授亞獻，亞獻執爵祭酒。

translations.literal: An attendant handed the cup to the secondary offerer; the secondary offerer took the cup and poured the libation.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant handed the cup to the secondary offerer, who took it and poured the libation.

sentences.zh: 三祭酒于茅苴，奠爵，執圭，俯伏，興，少退，再拜，訖，博士前導，亞獻詣次位行禮，並如上儀。

translations.literal: He poured three libations onto the thatched bundle, set down the cup, took up the tablet, prostrated himself, rose, withdrew slightly, bowed twice; when finished, the academicians led the way, and the secondary offerer proceeded to the next position to perform the rites, all according to the procedure above.
translations.idiomatic: He poured three libations onto the thatched bundle, set down the cup, and took up the tablet. He prostrated himself, rose, withdrew slightly, and bowed twice. When finished, the academicians led the way as the secondary offerer proceeded to the next position to perform the rites, all according to the procedure described above.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 終獻除本服執笏外，餘如亞獻之儀。

translations.literal: For the final offerer, except that he wore his regular robes and held the tablet, the rest followed the procedure for the secondary offerer.
translations.idiomatic: For the final offerer, except that he wore his regular robes and held the tablet, the rest followed the secondary offerer's procedure.

sentences.zh: 七祀功臣獻官行禮畢。

translations.literal: The offering officers for the meritorious officials of the seven sacrifices finished performing the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The offering officers for the meritorious officials of the seven sacrifices completed their rites.

sentences.zh: 太常卿跪奏：「請詣飲福位。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music knelt and reported: "Please proceed to the seat for receiving blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music knelt and reported, "Please proceed to the seat for receiving blessing."

sentences.zh: 」簾卷，出次，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The screen was raised; he left the pavilion; the court ensemble music began.
translations.idiomatic: The screen was raised. He left the pavilion, and the court ensemble music began.

sentences.zh: 殿中監跪進鎮圭，太常卿奏：「請皇帝執鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and presented the scepter of authority; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please let the emperor take up the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and presented the scepter of authority. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please let the emperor take up the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」前導，至阼階下，樂止。

translations.literal: Led forward, he reached the foot of the east steps; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Led forward, he reached the foot of the east steps, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 升自阼階，登歌樂作，將至飲福位，樂止。

translations.literal: He ascended by the east steps; the elevated choir music began; as he neared the seat for receiving blessing, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the east steps to the elevated choir music. As he neared the seat for receiving blessing, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 初，皇帝既獻訖，太祝分神位前三牲肉，各取前腳第二骨加於俎，又以籩取黍稷飯共置一籩，又酌上尊福酒合置一尊。

translations.literal: At the beginning, once the emperor had finished presenting the offerings, the Chief Invokers divided the meat of the three sacrificial animals before the spirit seats; from each they took the second bone of the foreleg and placed it on the tray; they also took millet and glutinous millet rice from the baskets and placed them together in one basket; they also poured the highest-grade blessing wine and combined it in one zun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, once the emperor had finished presenting the offerings, the Chief Invokers divided the meat of the three sacrificial animals before the spirit seats. From each they took the second bone of the foreleg and placed it on the tray. They also gathered millet and glutinous millet rice from the baskets into one basket, and poured the highest-grade blessing wine together into one zun.

sentences.zh: 又禮直官引司徒升自西階，東行，立於阼階上前楹間，北向。

translations.literal: The ritual officer also led the Minister over the Masses up by the west steps, eastward, to stand between the front pillars below the east steps, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer also led the Minister over the Masses up the west steps and eastward to stand between the front pillars below the east steps, facing north.

sentences.zh: 皇帝既至飲福位，西向立。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had reached the seat for receiving blessing, he stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor reached the seat for receiving blessing, he stood facing west.

sentences.zh: 登歌《福甯之樂》作。

translations.literal: The elevated choir performed the music "Funing."
translations.idiomatic: The elevated choir performed the music "Funing."

sentences.zh: 太祝酌福酒於爵，以奉侍中，侍中受爵捧以立，太常卿奏：「請皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The Chief Invoker poured blessing wine into the cup and presented it to the Palace Attendant; the Palace Attendant received the cup, held it, and stood; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please let the emperor bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invoker poured blessing wine into the cup and presented it to the Palace Attendant, who received the cup, held it, and stood. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please let the emperor bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」訖，奏：「請搢圭。

translations.literal: When finished, he reported: "Please tuck in the tablet."
translations.idiomatic: When finished, he reported, "Please tuck in the tablet."

sentences.zh: 」跪，侍中以爵北向跪以進，太常卿奏：「請執爵。

translations.literal: He knelt; the Palace Attendant, facing north, knelt and presented the cup; the Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take the cup."
translations.idiomatic: He knelt. The Palace Attendant knelt facing north and presented the cup. The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take the cup."

sentences.zh: 」三祭酒于沙池。

translations.literal: He poured three libations into the sand pit.
translations.idiomatic: He poured three libations into the sand pit.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「請啐酒。

translations.literal: He further reported: "Please sip the wine."
translations.idiomatic: He further reported, "Please sip the wine."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝啐酒，訖，以爵授侍中。

translations.literal: The emperor sipped the wine; when finished, he handed the cup to the Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sipped the wine. When finished, he handed the cup to the Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請受胙。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please receive the sacrificial meat."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please receive the sacrificial meat."

sentences.zh: 」太祝以黍稷飯籩授司徒，司徒跪奉進，皇帝受以授左右。

translations.literal: The Chief Invoker handed the basket of millet and glutinous millet rice to the Minister over the Masses; the Minister over the Masses knelt, bore it forward, and presented it; the emperor received it and handed it to attendants on his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invoker handed the basket of millet and glutinous millet rice to the Minister over the Masses, who knelt, bore it forward, and presented it. The emperor received it and handed it to attendants on his left and right.

sentences.zh: 太祝又以胙肉俎跪授司徒，司徒受俎訖跪進，皇帝受以授左右。

translations.literal: The Chief Invoker also knelt and handed the tray of sacrificial meat to the Minister over the Masses; the Minister over the Masses received the tray, then knelt and presented it; the emperor received it and handed it to attendants on his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invoker also knelt and handed the tray of sacrificial meat to the Minister over the Masses, who received the tray, then knelt and presented it. The emperor received it and handed it to attendants on his left and right.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒退立，侍中再以爵酒跪進。

translations.literal: The ritual officer led the Minister over the Masses back to stand; the Palace Attendant again knelt and presented the cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer led the Minister over the Masses back to his place. The Palace Attendant again knelt and presented the cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請皇帝受爵飲福。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please let the emperor receive the cup and drink the blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please let the emperor receive the cup and drink the blessing."

sentences.zh: 」飲福訖，侍中受虛爵以興，以授太祝。

translations.literal: When the blessing was drunk, the Palace Attendant received the empty cup, rose, and handed it to the Chief Invoker.
translations.idiomatic: When the blessing was drunk, the Palace Attendant received the empty cup, rose, and handed it to the Chief Invoker.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請執圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please take up the tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please take up the tablet."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself and rose.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「請皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: He further reported: "Please let the emperor bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: He further reported, "Please let the emperor bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」再拜訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the double bow was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the double bow was finished, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 太常卿前導，皇帝還版位，登歌樂作，俟至位，樂止。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music led the way; the emperor returned to the throne position; the elevated choir music began; when he reached the position, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music led the way as the emperor returned to the throne position. The elevated choir music began, and when he reached the position, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 太祝各進徹籩豆，登歌《豐甯之樂》作，卒徹，樂止。

translations.literal: Each Chief Invoker advanced and removed the baskets and bean vessels; the elevated choir performed the music "Fengning"; when the removal was complete, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Each Chief Invoker advanced to remove the baskets and bean vessels. The elevated choir performed the music "Fengning." When the removal was complete, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰：「賜胙行事，助祭官再拜。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman announced: "Sacrificial meat is bestowed for the rites; assisting sacrifice officials, bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman announced, "Sacrificial meat is bestowed for the rites. Assisting sacrifice officials, bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，在位官皆再拜，宮縣《來甯之樂》作，一成止。

translations.literal: Announcers transmitted the command; all officials in attendance bowed twice; the court ensemble performed the music "Laining" and stopped after one movement.
translations.idiomatic: Announcers transmitted the command, and all officials in attendance bowed twice. The court ensemble performed the music "Laining" through one movement before stopping.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「禮畢。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "The rites are finished."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "The rites are finished."

sentences.zh: 」前導，降自阼階，登歌樂止，宮縣樂作，出門，宮縣樂止，傘扇仗衛如常儀。

translations.literal: Led forward, he descended by the east steps; the elevated choir music stopped; the court ensemble music began; he went out through the gate; the court ensemble music stopped; umbrellas, fans, and guards attended according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Led forward, he descended the east steps. The elevated choir music stopped and the court ensemble music began. He went out through the gate, the court ensemble music ceased, and umbrellas, fans, and guards attended according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「請釋鎮圭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music reported: "Please release the scepter of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music reported, "Please release the scepter of authority."

sentences.zh: 」殿中監跪受鎮圭，皇帝還大次。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt and received the scepter of authority; the emperor returned to the grand rest pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The Superintendent of the Palace knelt to receive the scepter of authority, and the emperor returned to the grand rest pavilion.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人、禮直官、贊者各引享官、宗室子孫及從享群官，以次出。

translations.literal: Protocol ushers, ritual officers, and announcers each led the sacrifice officiants, imperial clansmen and descendants, and assisting officials sharing the offering out in order.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol ushers, ritual officers, and announcers each led the sacrifice officiants, imperial clansmen and descendants, and assisting officials sharing the offering out in order.

sentences.zh: 及引導駕官東神門外大次前祗候，前導如常儀。

translations.literal: They also led the procession guides to await respectfully before the grand rest pavilion outside the east spirit gate, and led the way forward according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: They also led the procession guides to await respectfully before the grand rest pavilion outside the east spirit gate, then led the way forward according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 贊者引御史已下俱複執事位，立定。

translations.literal: Announcers led the censor and all below him back to their duty positions, where they stood in place.
translations.idiomatic: Announcers led the censor and all officials below him back to their duty positions, where they stood in place.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman announced: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman announced, "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜。

translations.literal: All bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: All bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊者引工人、舞人以次出。

translations.literal: Announcers led the musicians and dancers out in order.
translations.idiomatic: Announcers led the musicians and dancers out in order.

sentences.zh: 大禮使帥諸禮官、太廟令、太祝、官闈令，升納神主如常儀。

translations.literal: The Grand Ritual Envoy led the ritual officials, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, the Chief Invokers, and the Director of Palace Environs up to store the spirit tablets according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ritual Envoy led the ritual officials, the Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple, the Chief Invokers, and the Director of Palace Environs up to store the spirit tablets according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，禮直官引大禮使已下降自西階，至橫街，再拜而退。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the ritual officer led the Grand Ritual Envoy and those below him down by the west steps to the cross street, where they bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the ritual officer led the Grand Ritual Envoy and those below him down the west steps to the cross street, where they bowed twice and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其祝冊藏於匱。

translations.literal: The prayer register was stored in the casket.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer register was stored in the casket.

sentences.zh: 七祀功臣分奠，如祫享之儀。

translations.literal: Separate offerings for the meritorious officials of the seven sacrifices followed the procedure for the jia offering.
translations.idiomatic: Separate offerings for the meritorious officials of the seven sacrifices followed the jia offering procedure.

sentences.zh: 時享儀

translations.literal: Ritual for the Seasonal Offering
translations.idiomatic: Ritual for the Seasonal Offering

sentences.zh: 有司行事。

translations.literal: The responsible officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 前期，太常寺舉申禮部，關學士院司天堂台，擇日。

translations.literal: In advance, the Ministry of Ritual Music submitted a report to the Ministry of Rites, notified the Hanlin Academy and the Celestial Observatory, and selected a date.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, the Ministry of Ritual Music reported to the Ministry of Rites, notified the Hanlin Academy and the Celestial Observatory, and chose a date.

sentences.zh: 以其日報太常寺。

translations.literal: The chosen date was reported to the Ministry of Ritual Music.
translations.idiomatic: The chosen date was reported to the Ministry of Ritual Music.

sentences.zh: 前七日，受誓戒於尚書省。

translations.literal: Seven days beforehand, the oath of purification was received at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days beforehand, the oath of purification was taken at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 其日質明，禮直官設位版於都堂之下，依已定《誓戒圖》，禮直官引三獻官，並應行事執事官等，各就位，立定，贊：「揖。

translations.literal: At dawn on that day, ritual officers set name placards below the main hall according to the established Oath of Purification Diagram; ritual officers led the three offering officers and all attending ritual officials to their positions, had them stand in place, and announced: "Bow with joined hands."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on that day, ritual officers set name placards below the main hall according to the established Oath of Purification Diagram. They then led the three offering officers and all attending ritual officials to their positions. Once all stood in place, the announcer called, "Bow with joined hands."

sentences.zh: 」在位官皆對揖，訖，禮直官以誓文奉初獻官，初獻官搢笏，讀誓文：「某月，某日，孟春，薦享太廟，各揚其職。

translations.literal: All officials in position bowed with joined hands to one another; when finished, the ritual officer presented the oath text to the primary offerer; the primary offerer tucked in his tablet and read the oath text: "On such-and-such month, on such-and-such day, in early spring, we shall present offerings at the Grand Ancestral Temple; each man shall fulfill his duty."
translations.idiomatic: All officials in position bowed with joined hands to one another. When that was finished, the ritual officer presented the oath text to the primary offerer. The primary offerer tucked in his tablet and read the oath: "On such-and-such month, on such-and-such day, in early spring, we shall present offerings at the Grand Ancestral Temple. Each man shall fulfill his duty."

sentences.zh: 不恭其事，國有常刑。

translations.literal: Whoever is not reverent in his duties shall face the fixed punishments of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever is not reverent in his duties shall face the fixed punishments of the state.

sentences.zh: 」讀訖，執笏。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, he took up his tablet.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, he took up his tablet.

sentences.zh: 七品以下官先退，餘官對拜訖乃退。

translations.literal: Officials of seventh rank and below withdrew first; the remaining officials bowed to one another and only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of seventh rank and below withdrew first. The remaining officials bowed to one another and only then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 散齋四日，治事如故，宿於正寢，唯不弔喪、問疾、作樂、判署刑殺文字決罰罪人及預穢惡。

translations.literal: For four days of general purification they continued managing affairs as usual and slept in their proper quarters, but did not offer condolences, inquire after the sick, engage in music, sign documents involving capital punishment, pass judgment on criminals, or participate in defilement.
translations.idiomatic: During four days of general purification they continued managing affairs as usual and slept in their proper quarters, but they did not offer condolences, inquire after the sick, engage in music, sign documents involving capital punishment, pass judgment on criminals, or participate in anything defiling.

sentences.zh: 致齋，三日于本司，唯享事得行，其餘悉禁，一日於享所。

translations.literal: For strict purification, three days at one's own office with only offering duties permitted and all else forbidden, and one day at the offering site.
translations.idiomatic: For strict purification, they spent three days at their own offices, permitted to perform only offering duties while all else was forbidden, and one day at the offering site.

sentences.zh: 已齋而闕者，通攝行事。

translations.literal: Those who had completed purification but were absent were collectively deputized to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had completed purification but were absent were collectively deputized to perform the rites in their stead.

sentences.zh: 前三日，兵部量設兵衛，列於廟之四門。

translations.literal: Three days before, the Ministry of War measured out and posted guards at all four gates of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Three days beforehand, the Ministry of War measured out the ground and posted guards at all four gates of the temple.

sentences.zh: 前一日，禁斷行人。

translations.literal: One day before, passage was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: One day beforehand, passage through the temple precinct was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 儀鸞司設饌幔十一所于南神門外西，南向。

translations.literal: The Palace Ceremonial Office set up eleven food pavilions west of the outside of the South Spirit Gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: West of the outside of the South Spirit Gate, the Palace Ceremonial Office erected eleven food pavilions facing south.

sentences.zh: 又設七祀司命、戶二位於橫街之北，道西，東向。

translations.literal: Positions for the Director of Fate and Household of the seven sacrifices were also set north of the cross street, west of the path, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Positions for the Director of Fate and Household of the seven sacrifices were also set north of the cross street, west of the path, facing east.

sentences.zh: 又設群官齋宿次於廟門之東西舍。

translations.literal: Lodging quarters for fasting officials were also set in the east and west side-buildings of the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging quarters for the fasting officials were also set up in the east and west side-buildings of the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 前二日，大樂局設登歌之樂於殿上。

translations.literal: Two days before, the Bureau of Great Music set up the ascending-song ensemble on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Two days beforehand, the Bureau of Great Music set up the ascending-song ensemble on the hall.

sentences.zh: 太廟令帥其屬，掃除廟殿門之內外，於室內鋪設神位於北墉下，當戶南向。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his subordinates to sweep inside and outside the temple hall and gates; within each chamber spirit seats were laid out below the north wall, facing south toward the door.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his staff in sweeping the temple hall and gates inside and out. Within each chamber, spirit seats were laid out below the north wall, facing south toward the door.

sentences.zh: 設幾於筵上，又設三獻官拜褥位二。

translations.literal: Tables were set on the mats, and two kneeling cushions were also set for the three offering officers.
translations.idiomatic: Tables were placed on the mats, and two kneeling cushions were also set for the three offering officers.

sentences.zh: 一在室內，一在室外。

translations.literal: One inside the chamber, one outside.
translations.idiomatic: One was inside the chamber, one outside.

sentences.zh: 學士院定撰祝文訖，計會通進司請禦署，降付禮部，置於祝案。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academy had finalized the prayer text, it coordinated with the Communication Bureau to request the imperial signature; the text was transmitted down to the Ministry of Rites and placed on the prayer table.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academy had finalized the prayer text, it coordinated with the Communication Bureau to request the imperial signature. The text was then transmitted to the Ministry of Rites and placed on the prayer table.

sentences.zh: 祠祭局濯溉祭器與尊彝訖，鋪設如儀。

translations.literal: The Sacrificial Ritual Bureau washed and rinsed the ritual vessels and zun-yi, and when finished set them out according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrificial Ritual Bureau washed and rinsed the ritual vessels and zun-yi, then set them out according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 內太尊二、山罍二在室。

translations.literal: Two inner grand zun and two mountain lei were placed in the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Two inner grand zun and two mountain lei were placed in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 犧尊五、象尊五、雞彝一、鳥彝一在室戶外之左，爐炭稍前。

translations.literal: Five sacrificial zun, five elephant zun, one rooster yi, and one bird yi were placed to the left outside the chamber door, with the brazier coals slightly forward.
translations.idiomatic: Five sacrificial zun, five elephant zun, one rooster yi, and one bird yi were placed to the left outside the chamber door, with the brazier coals set slightly forward.

sentences.zh: 著尊二、犧尊二在殿上，象尊二、壺尊六在下。

translations.literal: Two ceremonial zun and two sacrificial zun on the hall; two elephant zun and six pot zun below.
translations.idiomatic: Two ceremonial zun and two sacrificial zun were placed on the hall; two elephant zun and six pot zun below.

sentences.zh: 俱北向西上，加冪，皆設而不酌。

translations.literal: All faced north in west-upper order, covers were placed on them, and all were set out but not yet filled.
translations.idiomatic: All faced north in west-upper order, covers were placed on them, and all were set out but not yet filled.

sentences.zh: 並設獻官罍洗位。

translations.literal: Washing stations for the offering officers' lei were also set up.
translations.idiomatic: Washing stations for the offering officers' lei were also set up.

sentences.zh: 禮部設祝案於室戶外之右。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites set the prayer table to the right outside the chamber door.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites set the prayer table to the right outside the chamber door.

sentences.zh: 禮直官設位版並省牲位，如式。

translations.literal: Ritual officers set name placards and the sacrificial inspection station according to the prescribed form.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers set name placards and the sacrificial inspection station according to the prescribed form.

sentences.zh: 前一日，諸太祝與廩犧令以牲就東神門外。

translations.literal: One day before, all Chief Invokers and the Director of Sacrificial Livestock brought the sacrificial animals to outside the East Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: One day beforehand, the Chief Invokers and the Director of Sacrificial Livestock brought the sacrificial animals to outside the East Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 司尊彝與禮直官及執事皆入，升自西階，以俟。

translations.literal: The vessel custodian, ritual officers, and attendants all entered and ascended by the west steps to await.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel custodian, ritual officers, and attendants all entered and ascended the west steps to await the inspection.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿，贊者引御史，自西階升，遍視滌濯。

translations.literal: The ritual officer led the Minister of Ritual Music; the announcer led the censor; they ascended by the west steps and inspected all washing and rinsing.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer led the Minister of Ritual Music, and the announcer led the censor; they ascended the west steps and inspected all the washing and rinsing.

sentences.zh: 執尊者舉冪告潔，訖，引降就省牲位。

translations.literal: The zun bearer raised the cover and reported purity; when finished, they were led down to the sacrificial inspection station.
translations.idiomatic: The zun bearer raised the cover and reported purity. When finished, they were led down to the sacrificial inspection station.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令少前，曰：「請省牲。

translations.literal: The Director of Sacrificial Livestock stepped slightly forward and said: "Please inspect the sacrificial animals."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Livestock stepped forward and said, "Please inspect the sacrificial animals."

sentences.zh: 」退復位。

translations.literal: He withdrew and returned to his position.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and returned to his position.

sentences.zh: 太常卿省牲，廩犧令及太祝巡牲告備，皆如郊社儀。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ritual Music inspected the sacrificial animals; the Director of Sacrificial Livestock and Chief Invokers circled the animals and reported completeness—all according to the suburban and altars ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ritual Music inspected the sacrificial animals. The Director of Sacrificial Livestock and the Chief Invokers circled the animals and reported completeness, all according to the suburban and altars ritual.

sentences.zh: 既畢，太祝與廩犧令以次牽牲詣廚，授太官令。

translations.literal: When finished, the Chief Invokers and Director of Sacrificial Livestock led the animals in order to the kitchen and handed them over to the Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspection was finished, the Chief Invokers and the Director of Sacrificial Livestock led the animals in order to the kitchen and handed them over to the Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 贊者引光祿卿詣廚，請省鼎鑊，申視滌溉。

translations.literal: The announcer led the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and pots and to examine the washing and rinsing.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer led the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and pots and examine the washing and rinsing.

sentences.zh: 贊者引御史詣廚，省饌具，訖，與太常卿等各還齋所。

translations.literal: The announcer led the censor to the kitchen to inspect the food provisions; when finished, they and the Minister of Ritual Music each returned to the fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer led the censor to the kitchen to inspect the food provisions. When finished, he and the Minister of Ritual Music each returned to the fasting quarters.

sentences.zh: 太官令帥宰人以鸞刀割牲，祝史各取毛血，每室共實一豆，又取肝惣共實一豆，置饌所，遂烹牲。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen led butchers to cut the animals with the bell knife; each invoker-historian took hair and blood, filling one shared bean vessel per chamber, also took the liver offering into one shared bean vessel, placed them at the food station, and then cooked the animals.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen led butchers to cut the animals with the bell knife. Each invoker-historian took hair and blood, filling one shared bean vessel per chamber, and also took the liver offering into one shared bean vessel. These were placed at the food station, and then the animals were cooked.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿帥其屬，入實祭器。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices led his subordinates to enter and fill the ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices led his staff to enter and fill the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 良醖令人實尊彝。

translations.literal: The Director of Fine Brew had the zun and yi filled.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Fine Brew had the zun and yi filled.

sentences.zh: 享日質明，百官各服其品服。

translations.literal: On the day of the offering, at dawn, all officials wore their rank-appropriate robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the offering, at dawn, all officials donned their rank-appropriate robes.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、贊者先引御史、博士、太廟令、太官令、諸太祝、祝史、司尊彝與執罍篚官等，入自南門，當階間，北面西上，立定。
